source.title: Endo-parameters for p-adic classical groups
source.authors: Robert Kurinczuk, Daniel Skodlerack and Shaun Stevens
source.read: arXiv v3 (31 August 2020, 'to appear in Inventiones Mathematicae'), 81 pages, PDF SHA-256 1cbcbb779d8d4ba8f3339d749b3dd7bc3d2555e6792491338a861d45009d9092, fetched 29 September 2026 and read in full by four readers in parallel (§§1–4, §§5–6, §§7–9, §§10–12 with Appendix A and the references), whose drafts were merged, deduplicated and checked. The published version (online 21 September 2020) was not compared; v3 is the accepted text. Locators are v3 statement numbers and pages. The independent review (REV-PAPER-KURINCZUK-SKODLERACK-STEVENS-21) read the version of record from the University of East Anglia repository copy (sourceVersions): it keeps the v3 numbering throughout, and printed page p is PDF page p − 596.
readSections: §6 Self-dual simple characters: intertwining and concordance
§8 Self-dual semisimple characters: intertwining and concordance
§10 Intertwining and conjugacy for special orthogonal groups
§11 Intertwining implies conjugacy for cuspidal types
Appendix A From skew to self-dual semisimple characters

summary: For a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group G° over a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p, and coefficients in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic different from p, the paper proves that two cuspidal types intertwine only if they are conjugate (Theorem 11.9), completing the classification of irreducible cuspidal C-representations of G° by conjugacy classes of cuspidal types begun by Stevens and Kurinczuk–Stevens. To do so it extends Bushnell and Henniart's potential simple characters and endo-equivalence to potential semisimple characters of general linear groups and to self-dual potential semisimple characters of classical groups (§§7–9), after a theory of ε-hermitian Witt groups, transfer and concordance of self-dual embeddings (§3), simple strata (§5) and the intertwining of self-dual simple and semisimple characters (§§6, 8, 10, Appendix A). It then defines (self-dual) endo-parameters and proves that they parametrize intertwining classes of full (self-dual) semisimple characters of GL_F(V) (Theorem 12.9), of U(V,h) (Theorem 12.29) and of special orthogonal groups (Corollary 12.34), and it conjectures a bijection between self-dual endo-parameters and wild Langlands parameters compatible with the local Langlands correspondence (§1.21), recorded here as a conjecture, not a target. The atlas plans smooth representations, compact induction and Mackey theory (SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.0–SR.2), local fields and Weil groups (Tau Ceti ClassFieldTheory and LocalFieldsRamification), hermitian Witt groups at stage level (GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.2) and the local Langlands correspondences (EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.6 for GL_m, ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.4 for classical groups): 21 of the 413 items are planned and 2 are in the libraries. Nothing plans strata, simple or semisimple characters, cuspidal types or endo-classes; these 369 items are routed to the Part II of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups on types and the construction of supercuspidal representations that PAPER-FINTZEN-21 proposed, as a separate branch for classical groups, with the transfer of ε-hermitian forms as a source of GN.2 and the parameter-side definitions as sources of LanglandsParameterStacks LP0 and ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.4.

items.name: §4 (restated §1.2, §1.6): the classical group G^o ⊆ G = U(V,h) and the standing setting
items.statement: Let F_o be a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p, F/F_o a quadratic or trivial extension with Gal(F/F_o) = ⟨x ↦ x̄⟩, ε = ±1, and (V,h) an ε-hermitian space over F/F_o. Put A = End_F(V), G̃ = Aut_F(V), and let a ↦ ā be the adjoint anti-involution of h on A (h(av,w) = h(v,āw)). The abstract group Σ = {1,σ} of order two acts on G̃ by σ(g) = (ḡ)^{-1} and on A by σ(a) = −ā. Set G := G̃^Σ = U(V,h) = {g ∈ G̃ : h(gv,gw) = h(v,w) for all v,w ∈ V}. G^o denotes the group of F_o-points of the connected component of the underlying reductive F_o-group, so G^o = G in the unitary (F ≠ F_o) and symplectic (F = F_o, ε = −1) cases and G^o = {g ∈ G : det g = 1} in the orthogonal case (F = F_o, ε = 1); G^o is called a classical group. Throughout the paper G^o ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o) ≅ F_o^×, C is an algebraically closed field of characteristic ≠ p, and a non-trivial character ψ_o of (F_o,+) of level one is fixed, with ψ = ψ_o ∘ Tr_{F/F_o}. The sign ε and F/F_o are fixed while V and h vary.
items.locator: §4, p. 21; restated in §1.2 and §1.6, pp. 2–3, arXiv:1611.02667v3
items.note: The introduction restates this; §4 is the formal definition. Library has only the bilinear special cases: tauceti:TauCeti.BilinForm.isometryGroup (isometry group of a bilinear form, covering the symplectic and orthogonal cases F = F_o), tauceti:TauCeti.QuadraticMap.orthogonalGroup and tauceti:TauCeti.QuadraticMap.specialOrthogonalGroup (the orthogonal case O(V,h) and SO(V,h)), mathlib:Matrix.symplecticGroup (matrix form). The unitary group of a hermitian form over a quadratic extension of p-adic fields, and the Σ-action formalism, are not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti, and no stage plans them. (SpinRepresentations layer 2 plans only the abstract orthogonal group, which is already in the library.)

items.name: External: realizations of one self-dual ps-character on (V,h) intertwine iff the embeddings are conjugate ([39, Theorem 5.2])
items.statement: Let (k,β) be a self-dual simple pair, Θ_− a self-dual ps-character supported on (k,β), and ((V,h),ϕ,Λ,r), ((V,h),ϕ′,Λ′,r′) ∈ Q_−(k,β). Then Θ_−((V,h),ϕ,Λ,r) intertwines with Θ_−((V,h),ϕ′,Λ′,r′) in G = U(V,h) if and only if ϕ and ϕ′ are conjugate in G.
items.note: Motivates concordance (Definition 3.25). Not in the atlas.

items.name: External: every smooth representation contains a full (self-dual) semisimple character (Dat [16, Propositions 7.5, 8.5])
items.statement: Standing hypotheses: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is a quadratic or trivial extension with Gal(F/F_o) generated by x ↦ x̄; C is an algebraically closed field of characteristic ℓ ≠ p and all representations are smooth on C-vector spaces; G^o is a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group (the F_o-points), G^o ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o) ≅ F_o^×. Every (non-zero) smooth representation of G̃ = GL_F(V) contains a full semisimple character, and every (non-zero) smooth representation of G^o contains a full self-dual semisimple character.
items.locator: §1.16, p. 6 (citing [16, Propositions 7.5, 8.5]); used again in §12.5 and for the map ϑ of §1.21, arXiv:1611.02667v3
items.note: Black box for the map ϑ : Irr(G^o) → EP(h,G^o). Not in the atlas.

items.name: External: Bushnell–Henniart Intertwining Theorem [9]: full simple characters intertwine iff endo-equivalent
items.statement: Two full simple characters of G̃ = GL_F(V) intertwine in G̃ if and only if they are endo-equivalent. Consequently intertwining of full simple characters is transitive, and simple endo-classes of degree dividing dim_F V parametrize the intertwining classes of full simple characters of G̃.
items.note: Black box generalized by Theorem 12.9. Nearest is the rejected PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17 SmoothRepresentationsPartII branch (/endo-class, /endo-distance), for GL_n only; that proposal was not accepted.

items.name: §1.20: Weil group, inertia, wild inertia, Weil–Deligne group and L-group of G^o
items.statement: W_{F_o} is the Weil group of F_o, I_{F_o} its inertia subgroup, and P_{F_o} the wild inertia subgroup (the pro-p Sylow subgroup of I_{F_o}). W′_{F_o} = W_{F_o} × SL_2(ℂ) is the Weil–Deligne group, and ^LG^o = Ĝ^o ⋊ W_{F_o} is the complex Langlands dual group of G^o. For a group H, Z(H) is its centre and C_H(X) the centralizer of a subgroup X.
items.note: The Weil group is ClassFieldTheory layer 9 (localWeilGroup, with Weil topology); inertia, and wild inertia as the pro-p Sylow subgroup of inertia, are LocalFieldsRamification layer 4; the semidirect L-group is ReductiveGroupsPartII RG2.5; LP0 uses Weil groups and wild inertia. The SL_2(ℂ) form of the Weil–Deligne group is not stated anywhere (ArithmeticGaloisRepresentations:R01.2 plans Weil–Deligne representations with a monodromy operator instead).

items.name: §1.21, (1.1): the centre of C_{^LG^o}(ρ) and the map from representations of S_ϱ to those of S_ρ
items.statement: Let ρ = ϱ|_{P_{F_o}} for a Langlands parameter ϱ. Then C_{^LG^o}(ρ) ≅ C_{Ĝ^o}(ρ) ⋊_{Ad ϱ} W_{F_o} (as in [18]), and Z(Ĝ^o)^{W_{F_o}} ≤ Z(C_{^LG^o}(ρ)) ≅ Z(C_{Ĝ^o}(ρ))^{ϱ(W_{F_o})} ≤ C_{Ĝ^o}(ϱ(W′_{F_o})), using that W_{F_o} has trivial centre and ϱ(SL_2(ℂ)) ⊆ C_{Ĝ^o}(ρ). Hence a representation of S_ϱ, viewed as a representation of C_{Ĝ^o}(ϱ(W′_{F_o})) trivial on C_{Ĝ^o}(ϱ(W′_{F_o}))° Z(Ĝ^o)^{W_{F_o}}, restricts to a representation of S_ρ.
items.note: Asserted with 'as in [18], we notice'; its proof is not given in the paper. Not in the atlas.

items.name: External (context): Yu's construction [45], Fintzen's exhaustion [20], Hakim–Murnaghan refactorization [22]
items.statement: Yu [45] constructs supercuspidal representations of a broad class of connected reductive F_o-groups H; Fintzen [20] proved that these exhaust all supercuspidal representations whenever the residual characteristic of F_o does not divide the order of the Weyl group of H; Hakim–Murnaghan [22] classify isomorphism classes of Yu's representations by equivalence classes of the data (refactorization).
items.note: Context only; not used in the paper. Covered by the proposed SmoothRepresentationsPartII (PAPER-FINTZEN-21, accepted proposal: Kim–Yu types, Yu's construction, exhaustion), which is not yet in the atlas; Hakim–Murnaghan refactorization is not proposed.

items.name: §2: local-field notation (o_E, p_E, k_E, val_E, U^n_E, N, T, e, f) and the coefficient field C
items.statement: Let F/F_o be an extension of locally compact non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p, of degree at most two, with Gal(F/F_o) generated by x ↦ x̄. For a finite extension E/F_o: o_E is its ring of integers, p_E the maximal ideal, k_E the residue field, val_E the additive valuation with image ℤ, and U^n_E = 1 + p^n_E for n ≥ 1. For a finite field extension E/L, N_{E/L} is the norm and T_{E/L} the trace; for non-archimedean local fields, e(E/L) is the ramification index and f(E/L) the residue degree. C is an algebraically closed field of characteristic ℓ ≠ p, and representations are smooth representations of locally compact topological groups on C-vector spaces. Σ = {1,σ} is an abstract group of order two.
items.note: Library pieces: mathlib:IsNonarchimedeanLocalField, mathlib:Algebra.norm, mathlib:Algebra.trace, mathlib:Ideal.ramificationIdx, mathlib:Ideal.inertiaDeg, tauceti:TauCeti.normalizedValuation (normalized valuation of a nonarchimedean local field). The unit filtration U^n_E (unitFiltration) and the intrinsic e and f of a finite extension of local fields are LocalFieldsRamification layers 0–1.

items.name: §2: intertwining sets I_g(ρ,ρ′) and I_G(ρ,ρ′)
items.statement: Let G be a locally compact topological group, H and H′ compact open subgroups, and ρ, ρ′ representations of H and H′ on C-vector spaces. For g ∈ G let ^gH = gHg^{-1} and ^gρ(x) = ρ(g^{-1}xg) for x ∈ ^gH, and put I_g(ρ,ρ′) = Hom_{^gH ∩ H′}(^gρ, ρ′) (a C-vector space) and I_G(ρ,ρ′) = {g ∈ G : I_g(ρ,ρ′) ≠ 0}. Then g intertwines ρ with ρ′ if I_g(ρ,ρ′) ≠ 0, and ρ intertwines with ρ′ in G if I_G(ρ,ρ′) ≠ ∅. Write I_G(ρ) = I_G(ρ,ρ).
items.note: Nearest: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.1 and SR.2 (Hecke algebras, compact induction, Mackey filtrations), which never define I_g. The finite-group analogue is tauceti RepresentationTheory/InductionRestriction layer 4. The paper writes '≠ ∅' where '≠ 0' is meant for I_g (see sourceIssues).

items.name: §2: symmetry of intertwining for characters or complex coefficients
items.statement: In the setting of §2, if C = ℂ, or if ρ and ρ′ are characters, then g ↦ g^{-1} restricts to a bijection I_G(ρ,ρ′) → I_G(ρ′,ρ); so intertwining is symmetric and one says ρ and ρ′ intertwine in G.
items.note: No proof is given in the paper. For C = ℂ it uses semisimplicity of finite-dimensional representations of compact groups (the representations in use are finite-dimensional); for characters it is immediate.

items.name: §3.1: E^even and E^odd
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) For E a finite extension of F_o, E^even = {x ∈ E^× : val_E(x) is even} and E^odd = {x ∈ E^× : val_E(x) is odd}.
items.note: Trivial once the normalized valuation (tauceti:TauCeti.normalizedValuation) is available. Not stated anywhere.

items.name: Lemma 3.1, (3.2): the norm group of a quadratic extension
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Suppose F/F_o is quadratic. Then N_{F/F_o}(F^×) = ((F^×)^2 ∩ F_o^even) ∪ ((−(F^×)^2) ∩ F_o^odd).
items.note: QuadraticFormInvariants 6C plans the norm criterion ((a,b)_K = 1 iff b is a norm from K(√a), item 2) and the closed Hilbert-symbol formula in odd residue characteristic for a general nonarchimedean local field (item 9). Together these determine N_{F/F_o}(F^×), but (3.2) itself is not a stated milestone. LocalFieldsRamification layer 2 plans the unramified norm group (mem_normGroup_iff_dvd_normalizedValuation). No library declaration.

items.name: Lemma 3.1(i): −1 is a square in F iff it is a norm
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Suppose F/F_o is quadratic. Then −1 ∈ (F^×)^2 if and only if −1 ∈ N_{F/F_o}(F^×).
items.note: Immediate from (3.2) (W2, planned via QuadraticFormInvariants 6C), but not stated anywhere.

items.name: Lemma 3.1(ii): if −1 is a square in F then the norms are the squares lying in F_o
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Suppose F/F_o is quadratic. If −1 ∈ (F^×)^2 then N_{F/F_o}(F^×) = (F^×)^2 ∩ F_o^×.
items.note: Immediate from (3.2); not stated anywhere.

items.name: Lemma 3.1(iii): norm group of the unramified quadratic extension
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) If F/F_o is quadratic and unramified then N_{F/F_o}(F^×) = F_o^even.
items.note: LocalFieldsRamification layer 2 plans the norm group of an unramified extension of degree f: normGroup, with mem_normGroup_iff_dvd_normalizedValuation (x is a norm iff f divides v(x)). Here f = 2.

items.name: Lemma 3.1, (3.3): norms of units from a quadratic extension
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Suppose F/F_o is quadratic. Then N_{F/F_o}(o_F^×) = (o_F^×)^2 ∩ F_o^×. (Proof via Hensel's lemma, 1 + p_{F_o} ⊆ (o_{F_o}^×)^2, and the residue-field statement N(k_F^×) = (k_F^×)^2 ∩ k_{F_o}^×.)
items.note: An intermediate step of the proof. It uses Hensel (W12a, library). LocalFieldsRamification layer 2 plans map_norm_unitFiltration_zero for the unramified case only.

items.name: §3.1: self-dual extension (E,β) of F/F_o and its fixed field E_o
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Let E = F[β] be a field extension of F with distinguished generator β. If the generator of Gal(F/F_o) extends to an involution x ↦ x̄ of E with β̄ = −β, then (E,β) is called a self-dual extension of F/F_o; E_o denotes the fixed field of this involution. If β ≠ 0 then E/E_o is quadratic (since β ∉ E_o).
items.note: Not in the atlas. Mathlib has field extensions and automorphisms (mathlib:IntermediateField, AlgEquiv) but not this notion.

items.name: Corollary 3.4: −1 is a square in E iff β² is a norm from E to E_o
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) If (E,β) is a self-dual extension of F/F_o with β ≠ 0, then −1 ∈ (E^×)^2 if and only if β² ∈ N_{E/E_o}(E^×).
items.note: Proof: Lemma 3.1 applied to the quadratic extension E/E_o; if −1 is not a square then E/E_o is ramified and val_E(β) is odd. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Lemma 3.5: norms through a self-dual extension
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Suppose F/F_o is quadratic. Let E_o/F_o be a finite extension, inside an algebraic closure of F, that does not contain F, and set E = F E_o. Then N_{E/E_o}(E^×) = {α ∈ E_o^× : N_{E_o/F_o}(α) ∈ N_{F/F_o}(F^×)}. Moreover, for α ∈ E_o, N_{E_o/F_o}(α) = N_{E/F}(α).
items.note: Reduces to the separable and purely inseparable cases (F_o may have positive characteristic); the separable case uses local class field theory (W10, planned). Not stated anywhere.

items.name: External: local class field theory, Artin reciprocity and base change
items.statement: (Local class field theory.) For a finite abelian extension L/K of non-archimedean local fields, inside a fixed separable closure, the Artin map induces an isomorphism Art_{L/K} : K^×/N_{L/K}(L^×) ≅ Gal(L/K). For the quadratic extensions E/E_o and F/F_o of Lemma 3.5 (E = F E_o separable over F), base change gives Res^E_F ∘ Art_{E/E_o} = Art_{F/F_o} ∘ N_{E_o/F_o} on E_o^×/N_{E/E_o}(E^×), and in particular N_{E/E_o}(E^×) has index two in E_o^×.
items.note: ClassFieldTheory layer 6 plans the finite local Artin isomorphism localArtinEquiv : K^×/N_{L/K}(L^×) ≃ Gal(L/K)^ab for every nonarchimedean local field. Layer 4 plans the Artin–Tate compatibility diagrams, including 'the norm to inclusion of Galois groups' (artinMap_groundNorm), which is the base-change identity used here.

items.name: Lemma 3.6: ramified self-dual extensions
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Suppose (E,β) is a self-dual extension of F/F_o with β ≠ 0 and ramification index e(E/E_o) = 2. Then val_E(β) is odd, and either (i) F = F_o, or (ii) F/F_o is quadratic ramified and e(E/F) is odd.
items.note: Elementary valuation argument; not in the atlas.

items.name: External: Hensel's lemma for square roots in local fields of odd residual characteristic
items.statement: Let K be a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic. Then 1 + p_K ⊆ (o_K^×)^2; consequently a unit u ∈ o_K^× is a square in K if and only if its image in k_K is a square.
items.locator: Proofs of Lemma 3.1 (p. 10) and Lemma 3.34(i) (p. 21), arXiv:1611.02667v3
items.note: tauceti:TauCeti.henselianLocalRing_integer makes 𝒪[K] a HenselianLocalRing for any IsNonarchimedeanLocalField K. tauceti:TauCeti.HenselianRing.exists_pow_eq_and_sub_one_mem_of_sub_one_mem (n = 2, invertible since p is odd) gives every w ≡ 1 mod 𝓂 as a square. The residue criterion follows in two lines, and QuadraticFormInvariants 6A/6C use it as 'Hensel's lemma'.

items.name: §3.2: ε-hermitian spaces over F/F_o, orthogonal sums, isometries and the monoid H^ε(F/F_o)
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Let ε = ±1. An ε-hermitian space over F/F_o is a finite-dimensional F-vector space V with a non-degenerate ε-hermitian form h : V × V → F, i.e. a non-degenerate sesquilinear form, linear in the second variable, with h(w,v) = ε·c(h(v,w)) for all v,w ∈ V, where c(x) = x̄ is the Galois conjugation of F/F_o. The orthogonal direct sum of (V_1,h_1) and (V_2,h_2) is V_1 ⊕ V_2 with h(v_1+v_2, w_1+w_2) = h_1(v_1,w_1) + h_2(v_2,w_2). An isometry (V,h) → (V′,h′) is an F-linear isomorphism f with h′(f(v),f(w)) = h(v,w); write h ≅ h′ if one exists. Orthogonal sums are compatible with isometry. H^ε(F/F_o) is the set of isometry classes, a monoid under orthogonal sum with identity the zero space.
items.note: Hermitian/ε-hermitian forms over a quadratic extension F/F_o (and skew-hermitian forms) are not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti: Mathlib has only the sesquilinear-form vocabulary (mathlib:LinearMap.IsSymm with a ring hom I, mathlib:LinearMap.IsAlt, mathlib:LinearMap.Nondegenerate, mathlib:LinearMap.IsAdjointPair), and Tau Ceti has the orthogonal special case F = F_o, ε = 1 as quadratic forms (tauceti:TauCeti.RegularFormClass, tauceti:TauCeti.hyperbolicPlane, tauceti:TauCeti.RegularFormClass.discr). GN.2 is a one-paragraph specification ('Integrate Witt groups, discriminants, Clifford/Hasse invariants, local classification … add … quaternionic/hermitian variants') with no packet nodes; QuadraticFormInvariants layers 1/4/6 cover only quadratic forms (the case F = F_o, ε = 1), and GlobalQuadraticForms is global (Hasse–Minkowski) with nothing local or hermitian. In this range the paper needs ε-hermitian forms only over commutative fields with involution (F/F_o and E/E_o), never over division algebras or skew fields.

items.name: §3.2: Gram matrices and the determinant det : H^ε(F/F_o) → F^×/N_F
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) The Gram matrix of (V,h) with respect to a basis v_1,…,v_n is J = (h(v_i,v_j)). It satisfies J̄^T = εJ (J̄ = entrywise Galois conjugate), a change of basis B replaces J by B̄^T J B, and det(J̄) = ε^{dim_F V} det(J). Put N_F = N_{F/F_o}(F^×) if F/F_o is quadratic and N_F = (F^×)^2 otherwise. The determinant det(V) = det(h) is the class of det(J) in F^×/N_F; it is well defined, depends only on the isometry class, and gives a morphism of monoids det : H^ε(F/F_o) → F^×/N_F.
items.note: GN.2 plans discriminants, including the hermitian variants. The orthogonal case F = F_o, ε = 1 is in the library as tauceti:TauCeti.RegularFormClass.discr and tauceti:TauCeti.RegularFormClass.discrHom (the discriminant as an additive map to the square-class group), and Mathlib has mathlib:LinearMap.toMatrix₂ for Gram matrices of sesquilinear maps. Hermitian/ε-hermitian forms over a quadratic extension F/F_o (and skew-hermitian forms) are not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti: Mathlib has only the sesquilinear-form vocabulary (mathlib:LinearMap.IsSymm with a ring hom I, mathlib:LinearMap.IsAlt, mathlib:LinearMap.Nondegenerate, mathlib:LinearMap.IsAdjointPair), and Tau Ceti has the orthogonal special case F = F_o, ε = 1 as quadratic forms (tauceti:TauCeti.RegularFormClass, tauceti:TauCeti.hyperbolicPlane, tauceti:TauCeti.RegularFormClass.discr). GN.2 is a one-paragraph specification ('Integrate Witt groups, discriminants, Clifford/Hasse invariants, local classification … add … quaternionic/hermitian variants') with no packet nodes; QuadraticFormInvariants layers 1/4/6 cover only quadratic forms (the case F = F_o, ε = 1), and GlobalQuadraticForms is global (Hasse–Minkowski) with nothing local or hermitian. In this range the paper needs ε-hermitian forms only over commutative fields with involution (F/F_o and E/E_o), never over division algebras or skew fields.

items.name: §3.2: isotropic and anisotropic spaces, the hyperbolic plane, hyperbolic spaces and complete polarizations
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) (V,h) is isotropic if h(v,v) = 0 for some non-zero v ∈ V, and anisotropic otherwise (the zero space is anisotropic). The hyperbolic plane (H,h_H) has basis e_{−1}, e_1 with h_H(e_{−1},e_1) = 1 and h_H(e_i,e_i) = 0 for i = ±1, so its Gram matrix is [[0,1],[ε,0]] and det(H) = (−ε)N_F. Up to isometry H is the unique two-dimensional isotropic ε-hermitian space. nH is the orthogonal sum of n copies of H. A space isometric to some nH is hyperbolic; hyperbolic spaces have a complete polarization V = V_1 ⊕ V_{−1} with V_{±1} totally isotropic.
items.note: Quadratic case in the library: tauceti:TauCeti.hyperbolicPlane, tauceti:TauCeti.hyperbolicClass, mathlib:QuadraticMap.Anisotropic, and QuadraticFormInvariants layer 1 (hyperbolic planes). The ε-hermitian and symplectic versions are only in GN.2's 'hermitian variants'.

items.name: §3.2 (text following Remark 3.8): one-dimensional spaces ⟨α⟩ and their isometry classes; anisotropic spaces are diagonalizable
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) One-dimensional ε-hermitian spaces are ⟨α⟩ (Gram matrix (α)) for α ∈ F^× with ᾱ = εα; there are none when F = F_o, ε = −1 (the symplectic case has no non-trivial anisotropic spaces). The isometry class of ⟨α⟩ is determined exactly by the coset of α in F^×/N_F. Hence the one-dimensional classes in H^ε(F/F_o) are: if F/F_o is quadratic, β ∈ F^× with β̄ = −β, and α ∈ F_o^× ∖ N_{F/F_o}(F^×): ⟨1⟩ and ⟨α⟩ for ε = 1, and ⟨β⟩ and ⟨βα⟩ for ε = −1; if F = F_o has uniformizer ϖ, α a non-square unit, and ε = 1: ⟨1⟩, ⟨α⟩, ⟨ϖ⟩, ⟨ϖα⟩. Every anisotropic space is an orthogonal direct sum of one-dimensional anisotropic subspaces, so it has a diagonal Gram matrix in a suitable basis.
items.note: The case F = F_o, ε = 1 (four square classes when p is odd) is QuadraticFormInvariants 6A (card_squareClasses_of_isUnit = 4), with diagonalization in the library (mathlib:LinearMap.BilinForm.exists_orthogonal_basis, tauceti:QuadraticMap.Nondegenerate.exists_orthogonal_basis). The hermitian cases fall under GN.2 only. Hermitian/ε-hermitian forms over a quadratic extension F/F_o (and skew-hermitian forms) are not in Mathlib or Tau Ceti: Mathlib has only the sesquilinear-form vocabulary (mathlib:LinearMap.IsSymm with a ring hom I, mathlib:LinearMap.IsAlt, mathlib:LinearMap.Nondegenerate, mathlib:LinearMap.IsAdjointPair), and Tau Ceti has the orthogonal special case F = F_o, ε = 1 as quadratic forms (tauceti:TauCeti.RegularFormClass, tauceti:TauCeti.hyperbolicPlane, tauceti:TauCeti.RegularFormClass.discr). GN.2 is a one-paragraph specification ('Integrate Witt groups, discriminants, Clifford/Hasse invariants, local classification … add … quaternionic/hermitian variants') with no packet nodes; QuadraticFormInvariants layers 1/4/6 cover only quadratic forms (the case F = F_o, ε = 1), and GlobalQuadraticForms is global (Hasse–Minkowski) with nothing local or hermitian. In this range the paper needs ε-hermitian forms only over commutative fields with involution (F/F_o and E/E_o), never over division algebras or skew fields.

items.name: Remark 3.9: the unique maximal anisotropic ε-hermitian space
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Up to isomorphism there is a unique maximal anisotropic ε-hermitian space over F/F_o; with the notation of Remark 3.8 it is ⟨1⟩ ⊕ ⟨−α⟩ if F/F_o is quadratic and ε = 1; ⟨β⟩ ⊕ ⟨−βα⟩ if F/F_o is quadratic and ε = −1; ⟨1⟩ ⊕ ⟨−α⟩ ⊕ ⟨ϖ⟩ ⊕ ⟨−ϖα⟩ if F = F_o and ε = 1; and 0 if F = F_o and ε = −1.
items.note: For F = F_o, ε = 1, QuadraticFormInvariants 6D plans u(K) = 4 and the uniqueness of the anisotropic quaternary form. The hermitian cases fall under GN.2 only.

items.name: Witt's theorem (§3.2): Witt decomposition of ε-hermitian spaces; Witt index, anisotropic class [h] and anisotropic dimension
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) For every ε-hermitian space (V,h) over F/F_o there is an isometry (V,h) ≅ n(H,h_H) ⊕ (V_an,h_an) with (V_an,h_an) anisotropic, and the Witt index n and the isometry class of (V_an,h_an) are uniquely determined by (V,h). [h] denotes the isometry class of (V_an,h_an) (the anisotropic class), and dim_an(V) = dim_F(V_an) the anisotropic dimension.
items.note: The orthogonal case (quadratic forms, 2 invertible) is in the library: tauceti:TauCeti.exists_nsmul_hyperbolicClass_add (existence), tauceti:TauCeti.eq_of_nsmul_hyperbolicClass_add_eq (uniqueness), tauceti:TauCeti.RegularFormClass.wittIndex, tauceti:TauCeti.RegularFormClass.anisotropicPart, and Witt cancellation tauceti:TauCeti.equivalent_of_equivalent_prod. There is no ε-hermitian or skew-hermitian (sesquilinear) version; only GN.2's 'hermitian variants' mentions one.

items.name: Remark 3.10: classification of ε-hermitian spaces in the unitary and symplectic cases
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) If F/F_o is quadratic, the isometry class of an ε-hermitian space (V,h) is uniquely determined by the pair (dim V, det V). If F = F_o and ε = −1 (the symplectic case), the isometry class of (V,h) is determined by dim V, which is necessarily even.
items.note: GN.2 plans the local classification with hermitian variants; no packet node. For the symplectic case the library has only a real-symplectic even-dimension fact (tauceti:TauCeti.SymplecticForm.even_finrank), and no classification over a general field. The orthogonal analogue (dim, d, Hasse invariant) is QuadraticFormInvariants 6D.

items.name: §3.3: the adjoint anti-involution and the isometry group U(V,h)
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) For an ε-hermitian space (V,h), the adjoint anti-involution a ↦ ā of End_F(V) is defined by h(av,w) = h(v,āw) for all v,w. U(V,h) = {a ∈ Aut_F(V) : āa = 1} is the group of isometries of (V,h). It is the group of F_o-points of a reductive F_o-group: a unitary group if F/F_o is quadratic, a symplectic group if F = F_o and ε = −1, and a full orthogonal group if F = F_o and ε = 1.
items.note: Library pieces: mathlib:LinearMap.IsAdjointPair (adjoints for sesquilinear maps), tauceti:TauCeti.BilinForm.isometryGroup (bilinear case, covering symplectic and orthogonal), tauceti:TauCeti.QuadraticMap.orthogonalGroup, mathlib:unitary (unitary elements of a star monoid, which would need End_F(V) with the adjoint as star). The unitary group of a hermitian form over a quadratic p-adic extension, and the structure as a reductive group, are not in the library or the atlas.

items.name: Remark 3.11: isometric spaces have isomorphic unitary groups, not conversely
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) If (V,h) and (V′,h′) are isometric ε-hermitian spaces over F/F_o, an isometry induces an isomorphism U(V,h) ≅ U(V′,h′). The converse fails: if F ≠ F_o and n is odd, there are two isometry classes of n-dimensional hermitian spaces over F/F_o, but their isometry groups are isomorphic.
items.note: The first half is trivial. The converse counterexample comes from scaling by a non-norm (det changes by α^n). Not in the atlas.

items.name: §3.3: the twisted form a^*(h)
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Let (V,h) be an ε-hermitian space and a ∈ End_F(V) with ā = ηa, η = ±1. Define a^*(h)(v,w) = h(v,aw). If a is invertible then (V,a^*(h)) is an ηε-hermitian space over F/F_o, and the adjoint anti-involution of a^*(h) is b ↦ a^{-1} b̄ a. In particular, for γ ∈ F^× with γ̄ = ηγ, the twisted form γ^*(h) makes sense for every ε-hermitian space.
items.note: An elementary construction, not in the library or the atlas.

items.name: §3.4: the Witt group W^ε(F/F_o)
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) W^ε(F/F_o) is the set of isometry classes of anisotropic ε-hermitian spaces over F/F_o, with the unique operation making H^ε(F/F_o) → W^ε(F/F_o), (V,h) ↦ [h], compatible with orthogonal sum. Its elements are also viewed as Witt towers (the fibres of that map). W^ε(F/F_o) is an abelian group: the inverse of the class of an anisotropic (V,h) is the class of (V,−h), and the identity 0 is the Witt tower of the hyperbolic spaces nH.
items.note: For quadratic forms, the Witt ring W(K) is QuadraticFormInvariants layer 4 (planned, not in the library: only the semiring tauceti:TauCeti.instCommSemiringRegularFormClass and cancellation tauceti:TauCeti.isLeftCancelAdd_regularFormClass exist). GN.2 ('Witt groups … hermitian variants') and GN.6 (Witt groups of exact categories with duality) are generic, with no packet nodes. The ε-hermitian Witt group over F/F_o is not stated anywhere concretely.

items.name: Proposition 3.12(i): the unitary Witt group has order 4
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) If F/F_o is quadratic then W^ε(F/F_o) has order 4, and W^ε(F/F_o) ≅ C_2 × C_2 if −1 ∈ N_F, and W^ε(F/F_o) ≅ C_4 otherwise.
items.note: Only GN.2 ('Witt groups … local classification … hermitian variants') covers it, generically. No packet node; nothing in the library.

items.name: Proposition 3.12(ii): the symplectic Witt group is trivial
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) If F = F_o and ε = −1 then W^ε(F/F_o) is trivial.
items.note: Every non-degenerate alternating form is hyperbolic. GN.6 plans Witt groups of alternating forms generically; nothing in the library.

items.name: Proposition 3.12(iii): the Witt group of quadratic forms over F_o has order 16
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) If F = F_o and ε = 1 then W^ε(F/F_o) has order 16, and it is ≅ C_2 × C_2 × C_2 × C_2 if −1 ∈ N_F = (F^×)^2, and ≅ C_4 × C_4 otherwise.
items.note: QuadraticFormInvariants layer 4 (W(K)) and 6D (classification by (dim, d, s); u(K) = 4) give the ingredients but state neither the order nor the group structure of W(K) for a local field; layer 4 excludes general torsion theorems for W(K). GN.2 ('Witt groups … local classification') is the generic owner.

items.name: §3.4: generation of W^ε by one-dimensional classes; ⟨1⟩ ⊕ ⟨1⟩ = 0 iff −1 ∈ N_F; the maximal element
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) W^ε(F/F_o) is generated by the classes of the one-dimensional anisotropic spaces ⟨α⟩. In W^1(F/F_o), ⟨1⟩ ⊕ ⟨1⟩ = 0 if and only if −1 ∈ N_F. The class of the unique maximal anisotropic space (Remark 3.9) is the maximal element of W^ε(F/F_o), i.e. the Witt tower of maximal anisotropic dimension.
items.note: For quadratic forms this follows from diagonalization and layer 4 of QuadraticFormInvariants. The hermitian case is only in GN.2 (generic).

items.name: §3.4: twisting isomorphisms γ^* : W^ε(F/F_o) → W^{εη}(F/F_o)
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) If γ ∈ F^× satisfies γ̄ = ηγ (η = ±1), twisting by γ, (V,h) ↦ (V,γ^*(h)), preserves orthogonal sums, isometries and hyperbolic spaces, so it induces a homomorphism γ^* : W^ε(F/F_o) → W^{εη}(F/F_o). This is an isomorphism with inverse (γ^{-1})^*.
items.note: Elementary, not in the atlas. For quadratic forms it is scaling by a unit (multiplication by ⟨γ⟩ in W(K), QuadraticFormInvariants layer 4).

items.name: §3.5: Galois-equivariant linear forms λ : E → F and the distinguished form λ_β
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Let (E,β) be a self-dual extension of F/F_o and n = [E:F]. A non-zero F-linear form λ : E → F is Galois-equivariant if λ(x̄) = c(λ(x)) for all x ∈ E (c = Galois conjugation of F/F_o); such forms exist, e.g. λ_β defined by λ_β(β^i) = 1 for i = 0 and λ_β(β^i) = 0 for 1 ≤ i ≤ n−1. Every non-trivial F-linear form on E can be written λ(x) = λ_β(γx) for a unique γ ∈ E^×, and λ is Galois-equivariant exactly when γ ∈ E_o^×.
items.note: QuadraticFormInvariants layer 9 plans 'Which functional': the non-zero elements of Hom_K(L,K) form an L^×-torsor. That is the non-equivariant half. The Galois-equivariant refinement (γ ∈ E_o^×) and λ_β are not planned.

items.name: §3.5: the transfer λ_* : H^ε(E/E_o) → H^ε(F/F_o) and λ_* : W^ε(E/E_o) → W^ε(F/F_o)
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Let E/F be a finite extension of degree n to which the Galois involution of F extends, with fixed field E_o, and let λ : E → F be a non-zero Galois-equivariant F-linear form. For an ε-hermitian space (V,h) over E/E_o, (V,λ ∘ h) is an ε-hermitian space over F/F_o, the transfer (V,λ_*h). Transfer preserves orthogonal sums and isometries, so it gives a morphism of monoids λ_* : H^ε(E/E_o) → H^ε(F/F_o). Since λ_*(H) = nH, it induces a group homomorphism λ_* : W^ε(E/E_o) → W^ε(F/F_o), which depends on λ.
items.note: The nearest plan is QuadraticFormInvariants layer 9, the Scharlau transfer s_*(q) = s ∘ q of quadratic forms along finite separable L/K, with isometry invariance and descent to W(L) → W(K). That covers only the case F = E_o = F_o-type symmetric forms, not ε-hermitian forms over E/E_o with Galois-equivariant functionals, nor inseparable E/F. Nothing in the library (no scharlauTransfer declaration).

items.name: Proposition 3.13(i): the image of the transfer is independent of λ
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Let (E,β) be a self-dual extension of F/F_o. The image λ_*(W^ε(E/E_o)) ⊆ W^ε(F/F_o) is independent of the choice of the non-zero Galois-equivariant F-linear form λ. (Indeed λ = λ′(γ·) with γ ∈ E_o^×, so λ_* = λ′_* ∘ γ^* and γ^* is an isomorphism.)
items.note: The quadratic-form analogue ('change of functional (λ·s)_*q ≅ s_*(⟨λ⟩ ⊗ q)') is planned in QuadraticFormInvariants layer 9. The hermitian statement is not planned.

items.name: Proposition 3.13(ii): transfer sends the maximal element to the maximal element
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Let (E,β) be a self-dual extension of F/F_o. For every non-zero Galois-equivariant F-linear form λ : E → F, λ_* sends the maximal element of W^ε(E/E_o) to the maximal element of W^ε(F/F_o).
items.note: Proved via [39, Theorem 4.4] (W32) for one λ, then by (i) since γ^* fixes the maximal element. Not in the atlas.

items.name: External: Skodlerack–Stevens [39, Theorem 4.4] (maximal Witt tower is preserved by a particular transfer)
items.statement: ([39, Theorem 4.4].) For a self-dual extension (E,β) of F/F_o and a particular non-zero Galois-equivariant F-linear form λ : E → F, the transfer λ_* : W^ε(E/E_o) → W^ε(F/F_o) maps the maximal element (the Witt tower of maximal anisotropic dimension) to the maximal element.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 3.13(ii), p. 15 (citing [39, Theorem 4.4]), arXiv:1611.02667v3
items.note: A black box; not in the atlas.

items.name: §3.5: W^ε_even(E/E_o) and W^ε_odd(E/E_o)
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) W^ε_even(E/E_o) ⊆ W^ε(E/E_o) is the subgroup of Witt towers of even anisotropic dimension. If W^ε(E/E_o) is non-trivial it has index two, and W^ε_odd(E/E_o) denotes its non-identity coset (the Witt towers of odd anisotropic dimension).
items.note: For quadratic forms, the dimension-mod-2 map W(K) → ZMod 2 is planned in QuadraticFormInvariants layer 4. The hermitian version is not planned.

items.name: Proposition 3.14: transfer is injective on each parity class outside the symplectic case
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Let (E,β) be a self-dual extension of F/F_o and suppose we are not in the symplectic case (F/F_o is quadratic or ε = 1). Then for every non-zero Galois-equivariant F-linear form λ : E → F, the restrictions of λ_* to W^ε_even(E/E_o) and to W^ε_odd(E/E_o) are both injective.
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 3.15(i): determinant of a transfer
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Let (E,β) be a self-dual extension of F/F_o, n = [E:F], and λ a non-zero Galois-equivariant F-linear form on E. For an ε-hermitian space (V,h) over E/E_o, det(λ_*(V)) = det(λ_*⟨1⟩)^{dim_E V} · N_{E/F}(det V) in F^×/N_F (here ⟨1⟩ is the one-dimensional hermitian space over E/E_o).
items.note: The quadratic-form analogue is Scharlau [31, Lemma 5.8] (W37). No plan states a determinant formula for transfers; QuadraticFormInvariants layer 9 plans only the transfer and Tr_*⟨1⟩.

items.name: Proposition 3.15(ii): the standard transfer λ_{β*} of ⟨1⟩ and ⟨β⟩
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Let (E,β) be a self-dual extension of F/F_o and n = [E:F]. In W^1(F/F_o): λ_{β*}(⟨1⟩) = ⟨1⟩ if n is odd, and λ_{β*}(⟨1⟩) = ⟨1⟩ ⊕ ⟨(−1)^{n/2+1} N_{E/F}(β)⟩ if n is even. In W^{−1}(F/F_o): λ_{β*}(⟨β⟩) = ⟨(−1)^{(n−1)/2} N_{E/F}(β)⟩ if n is odd, and λ_{β*}(⟨β⟩) = 0 if n is even. (More precisely λ_{β*}⟨1⟩ ≅ ((n−1)/2)H ⊕ ⟨1⟩ for n odd and ≅ ((n−2)/2)H ⊕ ⟨1⟩ ⊕ ⟨(−1)^{n/2+1}N_{E/F}(β)⟩ for n even.)
items.note: Checked against the displayed Gram matrix in the basis 1,β,…,β^{n−1}: its entries are (−1)^i λ_β(β^{i+j}), which vanish for 1 ≤ i+j ≤ n−1. The ε = −1 formula is only sketched ('similar'), and was checked independently via Proposition 3.15(i). Not in the atlas.

items.name: External: Scharlau [31, Lemma 5.8, Theorem 5.12], the quadratic-form analogues of Proposition 3.15
items.statement: (Scharlau [31, Ch. 2 §5].) For quadratic forms, the analogues of Proposition 3.15 hold: a formula for the determinant (discriminant) of a transfer s_*(q) along a finite extension L/K in terms of det(s_*⟨1⟩), dim q and N_{L/K}(det q), and the explicit computation of s_*⟨1⟩ for L = K(β) and the functional s(β^i) = δ_{i0} (0 ≤ i < n = [L:K]). The paper cites [31, Lemma 5.8, Theorem 5.12] for these without saying which result gives which.
items.locator: Proof of Proposition 3.15, p. 16 (citing [31, Lemma 5.8, Theorem 5.12]), arXiv:1611.02667v3
items.note: The paper uses these only as the quadratic model ('the hermitian case follows mutatis mutandis', with a sketch given for (ii)). QuadraticFormInvariants layer 9 plans the Scharlau transfer (citing Scharlau Ch. 2 §5) and the trace form Tr_*⟨1⟩, but not these determinant and λ_β-transfer formulas.

items.name: Remark 3.16: in the unitary case the standard transfer is fully determined
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) If F/F_o is quadratic, then, since isometry classes of ε-hermitian spaces are determined by dimension and determinant modulo N_F (Remark 3.10), Proposition 3.15 completely determines the standard transfer map λ_{β*} for every self-dual extension (E,β) of F/F_o.
items.note: A consequence of Remark 3.10 and Proposition 3.15. Not in the atlas.

items.name: §3.6: self-dual embeddings ϕ : E ↪ End_F(V), the E-space V_ϕ and the lifted form h_ϕ
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Let (E,β) be a self-dual extension of F/F_o, λ a fixed non-zero Galois-equivariant F-linear form on E, (V,h) an ε-hermitian space over F/F_o and A = End_F(V). An embedding ϕ : E ↪ A is self-dual if ϕ(x̄) = ϕ(x)^† for all x ∈ E, where a ↦ a^† (written ā in the paper) is the adjoint anti-involution of h on A. Then ϕ makes V an E-vector space V_ϕ. The F-linear map Hom_E(V_ϕ,E) → Hom_F(V,F), ψ ↦ λ ∘ ψ, is an isomorphism, so for each v ∈ V there is a unique ψ_v ∈ Hom_E(V_ϕ,E) with h(v,−) = λ ∘ ψ_v. Define h_ϕ : V_ϕ × V_ϕ → E by h_ϕ(v,w) = ψ_v(w).
items.note: Not in the atlas. Mathlib has trace-dual isomorphisms for field extensions but not this hermitian lift.

items.name: Lemma 3.17 ([6, Lemma 5.3]): h_ϕ is the unique ε-hermitian form with λ ∘ h_ϕ = h
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) In the situation of §3.6, h_ϕ : V_ϕ × V_ϕ → E is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian form over E/E_o, and it is the unique ε-hermitian form on V_ϕ with h(v,w) = λ(h_ϕ(v,w)) for all v,w ∈ V.
items.note: Taken from Broussous–Stevens [6]; the paper gives no proof. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Corollary 3.18 ([38, Proposition 1.3]): the lifted spaces are isometric iff the embeddings are U(V,h)-conjugate
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Let ϕ, ϕ′ : E ↪ A = End_F(V) be self-dual embeddings, with lifted ε-hermitian spaces (V_ϕ,h_ϕ) and (V_{ϕ′},h_{ϕ′}) over E/E_o (for the same λ). Then (V_ϕ,h_ϕ) and (V_{ϕ′},h_{ϕ′}) are isometric if and only if ϕ and ϕ′ are conjugate by an element of U(V,h).
items.note: Proof: an isometry V_ϕ → V_{ϕ′} is an element of U(V,h) conjugating ϕ to ϕ′, and conversely by the uniqueness in Lemma 3.17. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Remark 3.19: U(V,h)-orbits of self-dual embeddings correspond to a fibre of the transfer
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Suppose a self-dual embedding ϕ : E ↪ A exists. Since dim_E V_ϕ does not depend on the embedding, Corollary 3.18 identifies the U(V,h)-orbits of self-dual embeddings of E into A with the classes in the fibre of λ_* : W^ε(E/E_o) → W^ε(F/F_o) above [h] whose anisotropic dimension has the same parity as dim_E V_ϕ.
items.note: The paper omits the (here harmless) requirement that the anisotropic dimension be ≤ dim_E V_ϕ: when E ≠ E_o anisotropic dimensions are ≤ 2, and when E = E_o the fibre is a single class. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Remark 3.19(i): uniqueness of the orbit of self-dual embeddings outside the symplectic case
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) If a self-dual embedding of E into A = End_F(V) exists and we are not in the symplectic case (F/F_o quadratic or ε = 1), there is a unique U(V,h)-orbit of self-dual embeddings of E into A.
items.note: Follows from Proposition 3.14 and Remark 3.19. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Remark 3.19(ii): two orbits of self-dual embeddings in the symplectic case
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) In the symplectic case (F = F_o, ε = −1), if β ≠ 0 and a self-dual embedding of E into A = End_F(V) exists, there are precisely two U(V,h)-orbits of self-dual embeddings of E into A.
items.note: W^{−1}(F/F_o) = 0, and W^{−1}(E/E_o) has two classes of each parity. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Lemma 3.20: lifting commutes with twisting by β
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Let (V,h) be an ε-hermitian space over F/F_o, A = End_F(V), and ϕ : E ↪ A a self-dual embedding of the self-dual extension (E,β). Then β^*(h_ϕ) = (β^*h)_ϕ, an equality of (−ε)-hermitian E/E_o-forms on V_ϕ; on the right, β^*h denotes the twist of h by ϕ(β) (note that the adjoint of ϕ(β) is −ϕ(β)).
items.note: Immediate from the definitions and the uniqueness in Lemma 3.17. Not in the atlas.

items.name: §3.7: the comparison bijections w_{ε,β′,β} : W^ε(E/E_o) → W^ε(E′/E′_o)
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Let (E,β), (E′,β′) be self-dual extensions of F/F_o with β, β′ ≠ 0, so that W^ε(E/E_o) and W^ε(E′/E′_o) both have order four. w_{ε,β′,β} : W^ε(E/E_o) → W^ε(E′/E′_o) is the unique bijection that preserves anisotropic dimension and satisfies w_{−1,β′,β}(⟨β⟩) = ⟨β′⟩ and w_{1,β′,β}(⟨β²⟩) = ⟨β′²⟩. When β = β′ = 0 (so E = E′ = F), w_{ε,0,0} is the identity of W^ε(F/F_o). One writes w_ε when β, β′ are fixed.
items.note: Not in the atlas. Remark 3.22 explains that this choice, rather than ⟨1⟩ ↦ ⟨1⟩, is the one compatible with the transfers λ_{β*}, λ_{β′*}.

items.name: §3.7, (3.21): comparison maps are compatible with twisting
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) For self-dual extensions (E,β), (E′,β′) of F/F_o with β, β′ ≠ 0: β′^* ∘ w_{−1,β′,β} = w_{1,β′,β} ∘ β^* as maps W^{−1}(E/E_o) → W^1(E′/E′_o).
items.note: Stated without proof. Both sides are anisotropic-dimension-preserving bijections that send ⟨β⟩ to ⟨β′²⟩. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Lemma 3.23: when w_1 fixes ⟨1⟩
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Let (E,β), (E′,β′) be self-dual extensions of F/F_o with β, β′ ≠ 0. The following are equivalent: (i) w_{1,β′,β}(⟨1⟩) = ⟨1⟩; (ii) −1 lies in both (E^×)^2 and (E′^×)^2, or in neither; (iii) −1 ∈ (F^×)^2, or the residue degrees f(E/F) and f(E′/F) have the same parity.
items.note: (i)⇔(ii) follows from Corollary 3.4. (ii)⇔(iii) is the residue-field fact that −1 is a square in E iff −1 is a square in k_E. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Remark 3.24: comparison maps and lifted forms under an isomorphism f : E′ → E
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Suppose f : E′ → E is an F-linear field isomorphism with f(β′) = β. Then λ_{β′} = λ_β ∘ f, and w_{ε,β′,β} is induced by H^ε(E/E_o) → H^ε(E′/E′_o), (V_E,h_E) ↦ (V_E, f^{-1} ∘ h_E). Moreover, if ϕ : E ↪ End_F(V) is a self-dual embedding into an ε-hermitian F/F_o-space, then h_ϕ = f ∘ h_{ϕ∘f}, so w_{ε,β′,β}([h_ϕ]) = [h_{ϕ∘f}].
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Definition 3.25: (h,h′)-concordance of pairs (β,ϕ), (β′,ϕ′)
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Let (V,h), (V′,h′) be isometric ε-hermitian F/F_o-spaces, A = End_F(V), A′ = End_F(V′), (E,β), (E′,β′) self-dual extensions of F/F_o, and ϕ : E ↪ A, ϕ′ : E′ ↪ A′ self-dual embeddings, with [h_ϕ] ∈ W^ε(E/E_o) and [h′_{ϕ′}] ∈ W^ε(E′/E′_o) formed with λ_β and λ_{β′} (so λ_{β*}[h_ϕ] = [h] = [h′] = λ_{β′*}[h′_{ϕ′}]). The pairs (β,ϕ) and (β′,ϕ′) are (h,h′)-concordant (or just concordant if h = h′) if β and β′ are both zero or both non-zero, and w_{ε,β′,β}([h_ϕ]) = [h′_{ϕ′}].
items.note: The key new notion of §3. Not in the atlas or any proposal.

items.name: Remarks 3.26(i): concordance is an equivalence relation
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Concordance of pairs (β,ϕ) (Definition 3.25) is an equivalence relation.
items.note: The paper calls it 'immediate'. It uses w_{β″,β′} ∘ w_{β′,β} = w_{β″,β} and w_{β,β′} = w_{β′,β}^{-1}. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Remarks 3.26(ii): concordance with the same β is conjugacy
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) If β = β′ (so w_{ε,β,β} is the identity) and h = h′, then (β,ϕ) and (β,ϕ′) are concordant if and only if ϕ(β) and ϕ′(β) are conjugate by an element of U(V,h).
items.note: From Corollary 3.18 and Witt cancellation (equal Witt class and equal dimension imply isometric). Not in the atlas.

items.name: Remarks 3.26(iii): concordance via an isomorphism of fields is isometric conjugacy
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) If there is an isomorphism f : E′ → E with f(β′) = β, then (β,ϕ) and (β′,ϕ∘f) are concordant. Consequently (β,ϕ) and (β′,ϕ′) are (h,h′)-concordant if and only if there is an isometry (V,h) → (V′,h′) conjugating ϕ(β) to ϕ′(β′).
items.note: Proved from Remark 3.24 and (ii). Not in the atlas.

items.name: Lemma 3.27: concordance in a skew-hermitian space via the twisted hermitian forms
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Let (V,h) be a skew-hermitian (ε = −1) F/F_o-space, let (E,β), (E′,β′) be self-dual extensions with β, β′ ≠ 0 and ϕ : E ↪ End_F(V), ϕ′ : E′ ↪ End_F(V) self-dual embeddings, and suppose the spaces (V,β^*h) and (V,β′^*h) are isometric (β^*h, β′^*h the twists by ϕ(β), ϕ′(β′)). Then the following are equivalent: (i) (β,ϕ) and (β′,ϕ′) are concordant; (ii) (β,ϕ) and (β′,ϕ′) are (β^*h, β′^*h)-concordant.
items.note: Proof via Lemma 3.20, (3.21) and injectivity of β′^*. Not in the atlas.

items.name: §3.8: outside the symplectic case, concordance is equivalent to commutativity of (3.29) or (3.30)
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Outside the symplectic case, let (V,h), (V′,h′) be isometric ε-hermitian F/F_o-spaces, (E,β), (E′,β′) self-dual extensions with β, β′ ≠ 0, and ϕ : E ↪ End_F(V), ϕ′ : E′ ↪ End_F(V′) self-dual embeddings. Consider the diagrams (3.29): λ_{β′*} ∘ w_{ε,β′,β} = λ_{β*} on W^ε_odd(E/E_o), and (3.30): the same on W^ε_even(E/E_o). If dim_E V_ϕ and dim_{E′} V′_{ϕ′} have the same parity, then (β,ϕ) and (β′,ϕ′) are (h,h′)-concordant if and only if the diagram of that parity commutes.
items.note: Uses the injectivity of Proposition 3.14. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Lemma 3.31(i): diagram (3.30) always commutes
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Suppose ε = 1 and β, β′ are non-zero (self-dual extensions (E,β), (E′,β′) of F/F_o). Then diagram (3.30) (on W^1_even(E/E_o)) is always commutative.
items.note: The even classes are 0 and the maximal element, and Proposition 3.13(ii) sends maximal to maximal. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Lemma 3.31(ii): sufficient conditions for diagram (3.29) to commute
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Suppose ε = 1, β, β′ ≠ 0, w_1(⟨1⟩) = ⟨1⟩, [E:F] and [E′:F] have the same parity, and one of: (a) F ≠ F_o and [E:F] is odd; (b) F = F_o and there are extensions K/F ⊆ E and K′/F ⊆ E′, each invariant under the Galois involution but not fixed pointwise, with [E:K] and [E′:K′] of the same parity and a Galois-equivariant F-linear field isomorphism K → K′. Then diagram (3.29) (on W^1_odd(E/E_o)) is commutative.
items.note: The proof in case (b) uses the explicit transfer formula (3.32) and a group-order argument in W^1(F/F_o); checked. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Proposition 3.28: concordance for hermitian (ε = 1) spaces under parity conditions
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Let (V,h), (V′,h′) be isometric hermitian (ε = 1) F/F_o-spaces, A = End_F(V), A′ = End_F(V′), (E,β), (E′,β′) self-dual extensions with β, β′ ≠ 0, and ϕ : E ↪ A, ϕ′ : E′ ↪ A′ self-dual embeddings. Suppose dim_E V_ϕ and dim_{E′} V′_{ϕ′} have the same parity, and either (i) this common parity is even; or (ii) it is odd, w_1(⟨1⟩) = ⟨1⟩, and either (a) dim_F V is odd, or (b) F = F_o and there are an extension K/F contained in ϕ(E), invariant under the adjoint anti-involution of A but not fixed pointwise, and an isometry g : V → V′ with gKg^{-1} ⊆ ϕ′(E′). Then (β,ϕ) and (β′,ϕ′) are (h,h′)-concordant.
items.note: Derived from Lemma 3.31. In (ii)(a), F ≠ F_o is automatic, since F = F_o and β ≠ 0 force [E:F] to be even. Not in the atlas.

items.name: §3.9: the residual invariant y_β of a self-dual extension
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Fix a uniformizer ϖ_F of F, with ϖ̄_F = −ϖ_F if F ≠ F_o. For a self-dual extension (E,β) of F/F_o with β ≠ 0, let e = e(E/F), n = −val_E(β) and g = gcd(n,e), and let y_β be the image of ϖ_F^{n/g} β^{e/g} (a unit) in k_E. Also y_0 = 0 ∈ k_F.
items.note: Not in the atlas.

items.name: Definition 3.33: similar self-dual extensions
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Self-dual extensions (E,β) and (E′,β′) of F/F_o are similar if (i) f(E/F) = f(E′/F), e(E/F) = e(E′/F) and e(E/E_o) = e(E′/E′_o); (ii) val_E(β) = val_{E′}(β′); and (iii) there is a k_F-linear field isomorphism k_E → k_{E′} sending y_β to y_{β′}.
items.note: Used in Corollary 7.12 and §12. Not in the atlas.

items.name: §3.9: similarity does not depend on the choice of ϖ_F
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) The notion of similarity of self-dual extensions (Definition 3.33) is independent of the choice of the uniformizer ϖ_F (subject to ϖ̄_F = −ϖ_F when F ≠ F_o).
items.note: Stated without proof. Changing ϖ_F multiplies y_β and y_{β′} by the same element of k_F^×, because n, e, g agree for similar extensions. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Lemma 3.34(i): for similar extensions (F ≠ F_o), ϖ_F^{-1}β is a norm iff ϖ_F^{-1}β′ is
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Suppose F ≠ F_o and the self-dual extensions (E,β), (E′,β′) of F/F_o (β, β′ ≠ 0) are similar. Then ϖ_F^{-1}β ∈ N_{E/E_o}(E^×) if and only if ϖ_F^{-1}β′ ∈ N_{E′/E′_o}(E′^×).
items.note: Proof via Lemma 3.6, Hensel (W12a) and Lemma 3.1. Checked, including the implicit use that −1 is a square in k_E iff it is in k_{E′}. Not in the atlas.

items.name: Lemma 3.34(ii): for similar extensions (F ≠ F_o), diagrams (3.29) and (3.30) commute
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Suppose F ≠ F_o and (E,β), (E′,β′) are similar self-dual extensions of F/F_o with β, β′ ≠ 0. Then, for ε = ±1, the diagrams (3.29) and (3.30) are commutative, i.e. λ_{β′*} ∘ w_{ε,β′,β} = λ_{β*} on W^ε(E/E_o).
items.note: Corollary 5.20 (p. 30) removes the hypothesis F ≠ F_o; the §5 reader will list it. The proof uses Lemmas 3.5 and 3.23 and Proposition 3.15(ii). Not in the atlas.

items.name: Lemma 3.34(iii): similar extensions give concordant pairs (F ≠ F_o)
items.statement: (F/F_o as in §2: an extension of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with [F:F_o] ≤ 2 and Galois generator x ↦ x̄.) Suppose F ≠ F_o, let (V,h), (V′,h′) be isometric ε-hermitian F/F_o-spaces, A = End_F(V), A′ = End_F(V′), (E,β), (E′,β′) similar self-dual extensions with β, β′ ≠ 0, and ϕ : E ↪ A, ϕ′ : E′ ↪ A′ self-dual embeddings. Then (β,ϕ) and (β′,ϕ′) are (h,h′)-concordant.
items.note: Follows from (ii) and §3.8 (similarity forces [E:F] = [E′:F], hence dim_E V_ϕ = dim_{E′} V′_{ϕ′}). §3.9 says 'hermitian' but the lemma and its proof cover both signs of ε. Not in the atlas.

items.name: §4: σ-fixed subgroups J_− and skew/symmetric parts X_−, X_+
items.statement: In the setting of §4 (A = End_F(V), G̃ = Aut_F(V), Σ acting by σ(g) = ḡ^{-1} on G̃ and σ(a) = −ā on A): for a σ-stable subgroup J of G̃, J_− = J^Σ = J ∩ G. For a σ-stable o_F-submodule X of A, X_− = X^Σ = {x ∈ X : x̄ = −x} (the skew-symmetric elements) and X_+ = {x ∈ X : x̄ = x} (the symmetric elements).
items.note: Library pieces for bilinear forms: mathlib:LinearMap.skewAdjointSubmodule, mathlib:LinearMap.selfAdjointSubmodule, mathlib:skewAdjointLieSubalgebra. Nothing for the hermitian (sesquilinear over F/F_o) adjoint or the Σ-action formalism.

items.name: §4: A_− is the Lie algebra of G and G^o
items.statement: In the setting of §4, the space A_− = {a ∈ End_F(V) : ā = −a} of skew-symmetric elements is the Lie algebra of G = U(V,h) and of G^o.
items.note: Stated without proof (standard). In Mathlib, mathlib:skewAdjointLieSubalgebra gives the skew-adjoint Lie algebra of a bilinear form, but Lie algebras of algebraic groups over F_o are not connected to it. The Tau Ceti ReductiveGroups roadmap (layer 2: Lie algebra and adjoint representation) is generic.

items.name: Lattice sequences: o_F-lattice sequence, period, regular and strict (§5.1)
items.statement: Setting: F is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p (in the paper F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 of such fields), with ring of integers o_F, maximal ideal p_F, residue field k_F and a fixed uniformizer ϖ_F; V is a finite-dimensional F-vector space, A = End_F(V), G̃ = Aut_F(V). An o_F-lattice sequence in V is a map Λ from ℤ to the set of o_F-lattices in V which is decreasing and periodic: (i) Λ(k+1) ⊆ Λ(k) for all k ∈ ℤ; (ii) there is a positive integer e = e(Λ) = e(Λ|o_F) with p_F Λ(k) = Λ(k+e) for all k ∈ ℤ. The integer e is the o_F-period of Λ. Λ is regular if dim_{k_F}(Λ(k)/Λ(k+1)) is independent of k ∈ ℤ, and strict if Λ(k+1) ⊊ Λ(k) for all k ∈ ℤ.
items.note: Missing. Neither Mathlib nor Tau Ceti at the pinned commits has lattice sequences, hereditary orders, Bushnell–Kutzko strata or simple characters (declarations.tsv searched for hereditar*, latticeChain/LatticeSeq, Stratum, SimpleCharacter, parahoric: only unrelated names such as TauCeti.PlumbingGraph.latticeChainComplex and Mathlib's HahnEmbedding strata). Mathlib's Submodule.IsLattice (finitely generated o_F-submodule spanning V) is only a building block for the values Λ(k). No atlas stage or packet node states the notion: ReductiveGroupsPartII:RG2.2 plans 'the GL_n model from homothety classes of norms/lattice chains' of the building, which covers strict chains up to homothety but not ℤ-indexed periodic sequences with repetitions, their period, regularity, affine classes or the filtrations a_n(Λ); EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison:ET.6 asks only for 'the needed supercuspidal/type and segment theory' of GL_m(E), E/ℚ_p, and names no lattice sequences, strata or simple characters (the reviews of PAPER-FINTZEN-21 and PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17 read ET.6 as owning mixed-characteristic GL_m type theory, but this is not written into the stage). Proposed, not in atlas: PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17 route 2 to SmoothRepresentationsPartII (rejected in review) would build hereditary orders, simple strata, critical exponents, the Bushnell–Kutzko simple-character recursion and transfer for GL_n (its items hereditary-order, critical-exponent, stratum-equivalence, simple-characters, character-transfer); the accepted PAPER-FINTZEN-21 Part II uses Kim–Yu data and Moy–Prasad filtrations, not lattice-sequence strata.

items.name: Affine translation, affine class and direct sum of lattice sequences (§5.1)
items.statement: Setting: F is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p (in the paper F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 of such fields), with ring of integers o_F, maximal ideal p_F, residue field k_F and a fixed uniformizer ϖ_F; V is a finite-dimensional F-vector space, A = End_F(V), G̃ = Aut_F(V). For an o_F-lattice sequence Λ in V and a, b ∈ ℤ with a > 0, aΛ + b is the o_F-lattice sequence (aΛ + b)(r) = Λ(⌊(r − b)/a⌋), r ∈ ℤ, called an affine translation of Λ; lattice sequences Λ, Λ′ are in the same affine class if they have a common affine translation. The direct sum of o_F-lattice sequences Λ and Λ′ of the same o_F-period is (Λ ⊕ Λ′)(r) := Λ(r) ⊕ Λ′(r), r ∈ ℤ.
items.note: Missing: no lattice sequences, hereditary orders, strata or simple characters in Mathlib/Tau Ceti or in any atlas stage or packet (ET.6 only asks for unspecified GL_m 'supercuspidal/type' theory; RG2.2–RG2.3 plan buildings with a lattice-chain GL_n model and parahorics). Proposed only in the rejected PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17 GL_n branch to SmoothRepresentationsPartII (items hereditary-order, critical-exponent, stratum-equivalence, simple-characters, character-transfer); PAPER-FINTZEN-21 (Kim–Yu data) does not cover it.

items.name: Filtration a_n(Λ) of A and the valuation val_Λ (§5.1)
items.statement: Setting: F is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p (in the paper F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 of such fields), with ring of integers o_F, maximal ideal p_F, residue field k_F and a fixed uniformizer ϖ_F; V is a finite-dimensional F-vector space, A = End_F(V), G̃ = Aut_F(V). For an o_F-lattice sequence Λ in V and n ∈ ℤ put a_n(Λ) = {a ∈ A | aΛ(k) ⊆ Λ(k+n) for all k ∈ ℤ}; n ↦ a_n(Λ) is an o_F-lattice sequence in A. The valuation map val_Λ : A → ℤ ∪ {∞} is val_Λ(x) = sup{n ∈ ℤ | x ∈ a_n(Λ)}, with val_Λ(0) = ∞.
items.note: Missing: no lattice sequences, hereditary orders, strata or simple characters in Mathlib/Tau Ceti or in any atlas stage or packet (ET.6 only asks for unspecified GL_m 'supercuspidal/type' theory; RG2.2–RG2.3 plan buildings with a lattice-chain GL_n model and parahorics). items.name: a_0(Λ) is a hereditary order with Jacobson radical a_1(Λ) (§5.1, recalled)

items.name: Dual lattice, dual lattice sequence, self-dual lattice sequence (§5.1)
items.statement: Setting: F/F_o is an extension of degree at most 2 of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p, and x ↦ x̄ generates Gal(F/F_o); ε = ±1 and (V,h) is a finite-dimensional non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (h sesquilinear, linear in the second variable, h(w,v) = ε·conj(h(v,w))); A = End_F(V) with the adjoint anti-involution a ↦ ā of h, A_− = {a ∈ A : ā = −a}; G̃ = Aut_F(V) and G = U(V,h) = {g ∈ G̃ : gḡ = 1}, which is unitary if F ≠ F_o, symplectic if F = F_o and ε = −1, full orthogonal if F = F_o and ε = 1 (the paper's classical group G_o, the connected component, assumed ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o), plays no role here); σ acts on G̃ by σ(g) = ḡ^{−1}. For a self-dual extension (E,β) of F/F_o, E_o denotes the fixed field of the involution of E. For an o_F-lattice L in V, L^# = {v ∈ V | h(v, L) ⊆ p_F}. For an o_F-lattice sequence Λ in V the dual lattice sequence is Λ^#(r) = Λ(1 − r)^#, r ∈ ℤ, and Λ is self-dual if Λ^# = Λ + d for some d ∈ ℤ.
items.note: Mathlib's LinearMap.BilinForm.dualSubmodule (read at the pinned commit: {x | ∀ y ∈ N, B x y ∈ (1 : Submodule R S)}) is the dual with respect to o_F, not p_F, and for bilinear rather than sesquilinear forms, and there is no dual lattice sequence; Tau Ceti's IntegralLattice dual is over ℤ. items.name: Self-dual filtrations a_{n,−}(Λ), P_−(Λ), P^m_−(Λ) (§5.1)
items.statement: Setting: F/F_o is an extension of degree at most 2 of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p, and x ↦ x̄ generates Gal(F/F_o); ε = ±1 and (V,h) is a finite-dimensional non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (h sesquilinear, linear in the second variable, h(w,v) = ε·conj(h(v,w))); A = End_F(V) with the adjoint anti-involution a ↦ ā of h, A_− = {a ∈ A : ā = −a}; G̃ = Aut_F(V) and G = U(V,h) = {g ∈ G̃ : gḡ = 1}, which is unitary if F ≠ F_o, symplectic if F = F_o and ε = −1, full orthogonal if F = F_o and ε = 1 (the paper's classical group G_o, the connected component, assumed ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o), plays no role here); σ acts on G̃ by σ(g) = ḡ^{−1}. items.name: P(Λ) is parahoric in G̃; P_−(Λ) is the full stabilizer of a building point (§5.1, recalled)
items.statement: Setting: F/F_o is an extension of degree at most 2 of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p, and x ↦ x̄ generates Gal(F/F_o); ε = ±1 and (V,h) is a finite-dimensional non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (h sesquilinear, linear in the second variable, h(w,v) = ε·conj(h(v,w))); A = End_F(V) with the adjoint anti-involution a ↦ ā of h, A_− = {a ∈ A : ā = −a}; G̃ = Aut_F(V) and G = U(V,h) = {g ∈ G̃ : gḡ = 1}, which is unitary if F ≠ F_o, symplectic if F = F_o and ε = −1, full orthogonal if F = F_o and ε = 1 (the paper's classical group G_o, the connected component, assumed ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o), plays no role here); σ acts on G̃ by σ(g) = ḡ^{−1}. items.name: o_E-lattice sequences for a subfield E of A (§5.1)
items.statement: Setting: F is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p (in the paper F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 of such fields), with ring of integers o_F, maximal ideal p_F, residue field k_F and a fixed uniformizer ϖ_F; V is a finite-dimensional F-vector space, A = End_F(V), G̃ = Aut_F(V). Let E be a subfield of A containing F, so that V is an E-vector space. An o_E-lattice sequence in V is a lattice sequence of o_E-lattices in V (in the sense of §5.1 with o_E in place of o_F); these are exactly the o_F-lattice sequences in V which are normalized by E^×. For such Λ, e(Λ|o_E) is its o_E-period and e(Λ|o_F) = e(E/F)·e(Λ|o_E).
items.note: The last identity is implicit in the paper's usage (e.g. §6.1 transfer condition, proof of Corollary 6.9). items.name: Lemma 5.1: lattice sequences for fields with equal e and f are conjugate
items.statement: Setting: F is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p (in the paper F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 of such fields), with ring of integers o_F, maximal ideal p_F, residue field k_F and a fixed uniformizer ϖ_F; V is a finite-dimensional F-vector space, A = End_F(V), G̃ = Aut_F(V). Let E, E′ be subfields of A containing F with e(E/F) = e(E′/F) and f(E/F) = f(E′/F), and let Λ be an o_E-lattice sequence in V. Then there exist an o_{E′}-lattice sequence Λ′ in V and g ∈ G̃ such that gΛ′ = Λ.

items.name: The †-construction for lattice sequences and elements ([26, §4]) (§5.2)
items.statement: Setting: F is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p (in the paper F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 of such fields), with ring of integers o_F, maximal ideal p_F, residue field k_F and a fixed uniformizer ϖ_F; V is a finite-dimensional F-vector space, A = End_F(V), G̃ = Aut_F(V). Let Λ be an o_F-lattice sequence in V of o_F-period e = e(Λ). Put V† = V ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ V (e copies) and Λ† = ⊕_{k=0}^{e−1} (Λ − k), an o_F-lattice sequence in V†. Let A† = End_F(V†), M† the Levi subalgebra of A† stabilizing V† = V ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ V, M̃† its unit group (a Levi subgroup of G̃† = Aut_F(V†)), and for β ∈ A let β† = β ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ β ∈ M†. Then Λ† is a strict regular o_F-lattice sequence in V† of period e. For a stratum [Λ,n,r,β] in A, [Λ†,n,r,β†] is a stratum in A†.
items.note: Strictness/regularity are asserted (each quotient Λ†(k)/Λ†(k+1) has k_F-dimension dim_F V). items.name: The self-dual †-construction (§5.2)
items.statement: Setting: F/F_o is an extension of degree at most 2 of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p, and x ↦ x̄ generates Gal(F/F_o); ε = ±1 and (V,h) is a finite-dimensional non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (h sesquilinear, linear in the second variable, h(w,v) = ε·conj(h(v,w))); A = End_F(V) with the adjoint anti-involution a ↦ ā of h, A_− = {a ∈ A : ā = −a}; G̃ = Aut_F(V) and G = U(V,h) = {g ∈ G̃ : gḡ = 1}, which is unitary if F ≠ F_o, symplectic if F = F_o and ε = −1, full orthogonal if F = F_o and ε = 1 (the paper's classical group G_o, the connected component, assumed ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o), plays no role here); σ acts on G̃ by σ(g) = ḡ^{−1}. For a self-dual extension (E,β) of F/F_o, E_o denotes the fixed field of the involution of E. Let Λ be a self-dual o_F-lattice sequence in V with e = e(Λ). Let V† = V ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ V (2e copies indexed by j ∈ {±1, …, ±e}), write v = (v_j)_{j=−e}^{e} (j = 0 omitted), and define h†((v_j), (w_j)) = Σ_j h(v_j, w_{−j}). Define Λ† = ⊕_{j=1}^{e} (Λ − j) ⊕ ⊕_{j=1}^{e} (Λ − j)^#, with Λ − j in the j-th copy and (Λ − j)^# in the (−j)-th copy. Put A† = End_F(V†), G̃† = Aut_F(V†), M† the Levi subalgebra of A† stabilizing V† = V ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ V, β† = β ⊕ ⋯ ⊕ β ∈ M† for β ∈ A, G† = U(V†, h†), and g ↦ g† the diagonal map. For a self-dual stratum [Λ,n,r,β], [Λ†,n,r,β†] is its self-dual †-construction.

items.name: Properties of the self-dual †-construction (§5.2)
items.statement: Setting: F/F_o is an extension of degree at most 2 of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p, and x ↦ x̄ generates Gal(F/F_o); ε = ±1 and (V,h) is a finite-dimensional non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (h sesquilinear, linear in the second variable, h(w,v) = ε·conj(h(v,w))); A = End_F(V) with the adjoint anti-involution a ↦ ā of h, A_− = {a ∈ A : ā = −a}; G̃ = Aut_F(V) and G = U(V,h) = {g ∈ G̃ : gḡ = 1}, which is unitary if F ≠ F_o, symplectic if F = F_o and ε = −1, full orthogonal if F = F_o and ε = 1 (the paper's classical group G_o, the connected component, assumed ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o), plays no role here); σ acts on G̃ by σ(g) = ḡ^{−1}. For a self-dual extension (E,β) of F/F_o, E_o denotes the fixed field of the involution of E. In the self-dual †-construction for a self-dual o_F-lattice sequence Λ of period e: each copy of V is isotropic for h†, so (V†, h†) is a hyperbolic ε-hermitian space; Λ† is a regular strict o_F-lattice sequence in V† of period e with (Λ†)^# = Λ† (so self-dual with respect to h†); β† is skew whenever β ∈ A_−; and g ↦ g† is an embedding of G in G†.
items.note: Asserted without proof (direct computations; checked: (Λ†)^#(r) has j-th component Λ(r+j) and (−j)-th component Λ(1−r+j)^#). items.name: Conjugacy of self-dual regular strict lattice sequences ([38, Proposition 5.2], as invoked)
items.statement: Setting: F/F_o is an extension of degree at most 2 of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p, and x ↦ x̄ generates Gal(F/F_o); ε = ±1 and (V,h) is a finite-dimensional non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (h sesquilinear, linear in the second variable, h(w,v) = ε·conj(h(v,w))); A = End_F(V) with the adjoint anti-involution a ↦ ā of h, A_− = {a ∈ A : ā = −a}; G̃ = Aut_F(V) and G = U(V,h) = {g ∈ G̃ : gḡ = 1}, which is unitary if F ≠ F_o, symplectic if F = F_o and ε = −1, full orthogonal if F = F_o and ε = 1 (the paper's classical group G_o, the connected component, assumed ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o), plays no role here); σ acts on G̃ by σ(g) = ḡ^{−1}. For a self-dual extension (E,β) of F/F_o, E_o denotes the fixed field of the involution of E. As invoked in §5.2, in the proof of Corollary 5.20 and in the proof of Lemma 6.6: self-dual regular strict o_F-lattice sequences Λ, Λ′ of the same o_F-period in isometric ε-hermitian spaces, with the same duality normalisation (Λ^# = Λ and Λ′^# = Λ′, or Λ(0)^# = Λ(0) and Λ′(0)^# = Λ′(0)), are conjugate by an isometry. The normalisation cannot be dropped: in a symplectic plane with h(e_{−1}, e_1) = 1, Λ(k) = p_F^k(o_F e_1 ⊕ o_F e_{−1}) and Λ′(k) = p_F^k(o_F e_1 ⊕ p_F e_{−1}) are self-dual, regular and strict of period 1, but Λ^# = Λ while Λ′^# = Λ′ + 1. The shift d in Λ^# = Λ + d is preserved by isometries and changes by an even number under translation, so no isometry maps Λ to a translate of Λ′. The cases used are: the self-dual †-lattice sequences Λ†, Λ′† in (V†, h†) (for self-dual Λ, Λ′ with e(Λ) = e(Λ′)), which are conjugate in G†; and, in Corollary 5.20, regular self-dual lattice sequences Λ, Λ′ with e(Λ|o_F) = e(Λ′|o_F), Λ(0)^# = Λ(0), Λ′(0)^# = Λ′(0), in isometric spaces (V,h), (V′,h′), related by an isometry V → V′ sending Λ to Λ′.
items.locator: §5.2, p. 23; proof of Corollary 5.20, p. 30; proof of Lemma 6.6, p. 33, arXiv:1611.02667v3

items.name: Strata, depth, null strata and equivalence of strata (§5.3)
items.statement: Setting: F is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p (in the paper F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 of such fields), with ring of integers o_F, maximal ideal p_F, residue field k_F and a fixed uniformizer ϖ_F; V is a finite-dimensional F-vector space, A = End_F(V), G̃ = Aut_F(V). A stratum in A is a 4-tuple [Λ, n, r, β] with (i) Λ an o_F-lattice sequence in V, (ii) integers n ≥ r ≥ 0, (iii) β ∈ a_{−n}(Λ). Its depth is max{−val_Λ(β), r}/e(Λ). The stratum [Λ, r, r, 0] is a null stratum. Strata [Λ, n, r, β_1] and [Λ, n, r, β_2] are equivalent if β_1 − β_2 ∈ a_{−r}(Λ).

items.name: The element y_β, characteristic and minimal polynomial of a stratum, fundamental strata (§5.3)
items.statement: Setting: F is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p (in the paper F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 of such fields), with ring of integers o_F, maximal ideal p_F, residue field k_F and a fixed uniformizer ϖ_F; V is a finite-dimensional F-vector space, A = End_F(V), G̃ = Aut_F(V). items.name: Minimal element over F (§5.3; Bushnell–Kutzko)
items.statement: Setting: F is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p with fixed uniformizer ϖ_F; for a finite extension E/F, val_E is the normalized valuation, p_E the maximal ideal, k_E the residue field, U¹_E = 1 + p_E, e(E/F), f(E/F) the ramification index and residue degree. items.name: Self-dual and standard self-dual strata (§5.3)
items.statement: Setting: F/F_o is an extension of degree at most 2 of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p, and x ↦ x̄ generates Gal(F/F_o); ε = ±1 and (V,h) is a finite-dimensional non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (h sesquilinear, linear in the second variable, h(w,v) = ε·conj(h(v,w))); A = End_F(V) with the adjoint anti-involution a ↦ ā of h, A_− = {a ∈ A : ā = −a}; G̃ = Aut_F(V) and G = U(V,h) = {g ∈ G̃ : gḡ = 1}, which is unitary if F ≠ F_o, symplectic if F = F_o and ε = −1, full orthogonal if F = F_o and ε = 1 (the paper's classical group G_o, the connected component, assumed ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o), plays no role here); σ acts on G̃ by σ(g) = ḡ^{−1}. For a self-dual extension (E,β) of F/F_o, E_o denotes the fixed field of the involution of E. A stratum [Λ,n,r,β] in A is self-dual if Λ is a self-dual o_F-lattice sequence and β ∈ A_− (called skew strata in [43, Definition 2.1]; 'skew' is reserved here for Definition 8.3). A self-dual stratum is standard if Λ has even o_F-period and Λ = Λ^#.
