items.name: Lemma 5.4: equality of e(E/E_o) for G-intertwining self-dual simple strata
items.statement: Setting: F/F_o is an extension of degree at most 2 of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p, and x ↦ x̄ generates Gal(F/F_o); ε = ±1 and (V,h) is a finite-dimensional non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (h sesquilinear, linear in the second variable, h(w,v) = ε·conj(h(v,w))); A = End_F(V) with the adjoint anti-involution a ↦ ā of h, A_− = {a ∈ A : ā = −a}; G̃ = Aut_F(V) and G = U(V,h) = {g ∈ G̃ : gḡ = 1}, which is unitary if F ≠ F_o, symplectic if F = F_o and ε = −1, full orthogonal if F = F_o and ε = 1 (the paper's classical group G_o, the connected component, assumed ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o), plays no role here); σ acts on G̃ by σ(g) = ḡ^{−1}. For a self-dual extension (E,β) of F/F_o, E_o denotes the fixed field of the involution of E. Let [Λ,n,r,β] and [Λ′,n,r,β′] be self-dual simple strata in A which intertwine in G, and suppose e(Λ) = e(Λ′). Put E = F[β], E′ = F[β′]. Then e(E/E_o) = e(E′/E′_o).
items.note: Proof via the self-dual †-construction, [38, Proposition 5.2], [39, Theorem 8.5] (conjugacy up to equivalence) and [13, 5.2(i)] (equal residue-field images in a_0(Λ)/a_1(Λ)). items.name: Proposition 5.5: simple approximation of pure strata ([12, Theorem 2.4.1])
items.statement: Setting: F is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p (in the paper F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 of such fields), with ring of integers o_F, maximal ideal p_F, residue field k_F and a fixed uniformizer ϖ_F; V is a finite-dimensional F-vector space, A = End_F(V), G̃ = Aut_F(V). Let [Λ,n,r,β] be a pure stratum in A. Then there is a simple stratum [Λ,n,r,γ] equivalent to it and, for any such simple stratum, f(F[γ]/F) divides f(F[β]/F) and e(F[γ]/F) divides e(F[β]/F).
items.note: External black box (Bushnell–Kutzko [12], extended to lattice sequences). Applied to two equivalent simple strata it gives equal e and f ([12, 2.4.1(ii)], used in Lemma 5.2(ii)). Missing: no lattice sequences, hereditary orders, strata or simple characters in Mathlib/Tau Ceti or in any atlas stage or packet (ET.6 only asks for unspecified GL_m 'supercuspidal/type' theory; RG2.2–RG2.3 plan buildings with a lattice-chain GL_n model and parahorics). Proposed only in the rejected PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17 GL_n branch to SmoothRepresentationsPartII (items hereditary-order, critical-exponent, stratum-equivalence, simple-characters, character-transfer); PAPER-FINTZEN-21 (Kim–Yu data) does not cover it.

items.name: Notation 5.6: the canonical embedding ϕ_β of F[β] in A
items.statement: Setting: F is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p (in the paper F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 of such fields), with ring of integers o_F, maximal ideal p_F, residue field k_F and a fixed uniformizer ϖ_F; V is a finite-dimensional F-vector space, A = End_F(V), G̃ = Aut_F(V). For β ∈ A with E = F[β] a field, ϕ_β denotes the canonical embedding of E in A.
items.note: E = F[β] is Mathlib's Algebra.adjoin F {β} (the F-subalgebra of A generated by β; the hypothesis that it is a field is carried separately) and ϕ_β is its inclusion Subalgebra.val; both read at the pinned commit. Only the bare embedding is library; its self-duality (next item) is not.

items.name: A self-dual pure stratum gives a self-dual extension and a self-dual embedding (§5.3)
items.statement: Setting: F/F_o is an extension of degree at most 2 of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p, and x ↦ x̄ generates Gal(F/F_o); ε = ±1 and (V,h) is a finite-dimensional non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (h sesquilinear, linear in the second variable, h(w,v) = ε·conj(h(v,w))); A = End_F(V) with the adjoint anti-involution a ↦ ā of h, A_− = {a ∈ A : ā = −a}; G̃ = Aut_F(V) and G = U(V,h) = {g ∈ G̃ : gḡ = 1}, which is unitary if F ≠ F_o, symplectic if F = F_o and ε = −1, full orthogonal if F = F_o and ε = 1 (the paper's classical group G_o, the connected component, assumed ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o), plays no role here); σ acts on G̃ by σ(g) = ḡ^{−1}. For a self-dual extension (E,β) of F/F_o, E_o denotes the fixed field of the involution of E. If [Λ,n,r,β] is a self-dual pure stratum in A with E = F[β], then (E,β) is a self-dual extension of F/F_o (the Galois involution of F extends to E with β ↦ −β, namely the adjoint anti-involution restricted to E) and ϕ_β : E ↪ A is a self-dual embedding (ϕ_β(x̄) = conj(ϕ_β(x)) for the adjoint anti-involution).

items.name: Lemma 5.9: embedding a tame minimal field compatibly with leading terms (existence and uniqueness)
items.statement: Setting: F is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p with fixed uniformizer ϖ_F; for a finite extension E/F, val_E is the normalized valuation, p_E the maximal ideal, k_E the residue field, U¹_E = 1 + p_E, e(E/F), f(E/F) the ramification index and residue degree. Suppose E_1 = F[β_1] is a tamely ramified finite extension of F with β_1 minimal over F, and E_2/F is a finite extension with β_2 ∈ E_2^×. For i = 1, 2 write e_i = e(E_i/F) and n_i = val_{E_i}(β_i), and suppose (i) n_1/e_1 = n_2/e_2, and (ii) β_1^{e_1} ϖ_F^{−n_1} + p_{E_1} and β_2^{e_1} ϖ_F^{−n_1} + p_{E_2} have the same minimal polynomial over k_F. Then there is a unique F-embedding φ : E_1 → E_2 such that φ(β_1) β_2^{−1} ∈ U¹_{E_2} (5.10).
items.note: Proof checked: Hensel lifts of the common residue polynomial, reduction to E_1/F totally tamely ramified, e_1-th roots ξ_i, irreducibility of X^{e_1} − ϖ_F^{n_1}; uniqueness via a Bézout uniformizer and p ∤ e_1. Nearest: tauceti:TauCetiRoadmap/LocalFieldsRamification layer 3 (planned) defines IsTamelyRamified, proves that a totally tamely ramified L/K is K(α) with α^e = π, and records the degree of the maximal tamely ramified subextension; Tau Ceti already has TauCeti.unitFiltration (U^n_E) and Mathlib has Hensel's lemma. No stage, packet node or declaration states Bushnell–Kutzko minimal elements or this embedding/approximation result, so it is missing.

items.name: Lemma 5.9 (equivariance): the embedding φ is Galois-equivariant
items.statement: Setting: F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p with Galois involution x ↦ x̄ and fixed uniformizer ϖ_F. In the situation of Lemma 5.9 (E_1 = F[β_1] tamely ramified, β_1 minimal over F, β_2 ∈ E_2^×, n_1/e_1 = n_2/e_2, equal minimal polynomials of the residues of β_1^{e_1}ϖ_F^{−n_1} and β_2^{e_1}ϖ_F^{−n_1} over k_F), if moreover (E_1,β_1) and (E_2,β_2) are self-dual extensions of F/F_o, then the unique F-embedding φ with φ(β_1)β_2^{−1} ∈ U¹_{E_2} is equivariant: φ(x̄) = conj(φ(x)) for x ∈ E_1.
items.note: Proof: conj ∘ φ ∘ conj also satisfies (5.10), so equals φ by uniqueness. items.name: Lemma 5.11(i): tame approximation of a power of a minimal element
items.statement: Setting: F is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p with fixed uniformizer ϖ_F; for a finite extension E/F, val_E is the normalized valuation, p_E the maximal ideal, k_E the residue field, U¹_E = 1 + p_E, e(E/F), f(E/F) the ramification index and residue degree. items.name: Lemma 5.13(i): the tame part of an intertwining simple stratum embeds in E

items.name: Lemma 5.13(ii): same lattice sequence gives a conjugating element in P_−(Λ)
items.statement: Setting: F/F_o is an extension of degree at most 2 of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p, and x ↦ x̄ generates Gal(F/F_o); ε = ±1 and (V,h) is a finite-dimensional non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (h sesquilinear, linear in the second variable, h(w,v) = ε·conj(h(v,w))); A = End_F(V) with the adjoint anti-involution a ↦ ā of h, A_− = {a ∈ A : ā = −a}; G̃ = Aut_F(V) and G = U(V,h) = {g ∈ G̃ : gḡ = 1}, which is unitary if F ≠ F_o, symplectic if F = F_o and ε = −1, full orthogonal if F = F_o and ε = 1 (the paper's classical group G_o, the connected component, assumed ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o), plays no role here); σ acts on G̃ by σ(g) = ḡ^{−1}. For a self-dual extension (E,β) of F/F_o, E_o denotes the fixed field of the involution of E. items.name: Corollary 5.14: common tame self-dual subfield of intertwining pure strata
items.statement: Setting: F/F_o is an extension of degree at most 2 of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p, and x ↦ x̄ generates Gal(F/F_o); ε = ±1 and (V,h) is a finite-dimensional non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (h sesquilinear, linear in the second variable, h(w,v) = ε·conj(h(v,w))); A = End_F(V) with the adjoint anti-involution a ↦ ā of h, A_− = {a ∈ A : ā = −a}; G̃ = Aut_F(V) and G = U(V,h) = {g ∈ G̃ : gḡ = 1}, which is unitary if F ≠ F_o, symplectic if F = F_o and ε = −1, full orthogonal if F = F_o and ε = 1 (the paper's classical group G_o, the connected component, assumed ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o), plays no role here); σ acts on G̃ by σ(g) = ḡ^{−1}. For a self-dual extension (E,β) of F/F_o, E_o denotes the fixed field of the involution of E. Let [Λ,n,n−1,β] and [Λ′,n,n−1,β′] be self-dual pure strata in A which intertwine in G, E = F[β], E′ = F[β′], and let [Λ,n,n−1,γ], [Λ′,n,n−1,γ′] be self-dual simple strata in A equivalent to [Λ,n,n−1,β], [Λ′,n,n−1,β′] respectively. Moreover K can be chosen P_−(Λ)-conjugate to the maximal tamely ramified subextension of F[γ]/F, and if Λ = Λ′ one can take g ∈ P_−(Λ).

items.name: Lemma 5.15: concordance of intertwining strata in the symplectic case (parity condition)

items.statement: Setting: F/F_o is an extension of degree at most 2 of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p, and x ↦ x̄ generates Gal(F/F_o); ε = ±1 and (V,h) is a finite-dimensional non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (h sesquilinear, linear in the second variable, h(w,v) = ε·conj(h(v,w))); A = End_F(V) with the adjoint anti-involution a ↦ ā of h, A_− = {a ∈ A : ā = −a}; G̃ = Aut_F(V) and G = U(V,h) = {g ∈ G̃ : gḡ = 1}, which is unitary if F ≠ F_o, symplectic if F = F_o and ε = −1, full orthogonal if F = F_o and ε = 1 (the paper's classical group G_o, the connected component, assumed ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o), plays no role here); σ acts on G̃ by σ(g) = ḡ^{−1}. items.statement: Setting: F/F_o is an extension of degree at most 2 of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p, and x ↦ x̄ generates Gal(F/F_o); ε = ±1 and (V,h) is a finite-dimensional non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (h sesquilinear, linear in the second variable, h(w,v) = ε·conj(h(v,w))); A = End_F(V) with the adjoint anti-involution a ↦ ā of h, A_− = {a ∈ A : ā = −a}; G̃ = Aut_F(V) and G = U(V,h) = {g ∈ G̃ : gḡ = 1}, which is unitary if F ≠ F_o, symplectic if F = F_o and ε = −1, full orthogonal if F = F_o and ε = 1 (the paper's classical group G_o, the connected component, assumed ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o), plays no role here); σ acts on G̃ by σ(g) = ḡ^{−1}. For a self-dual extension (E,β) of F/F_o, E_o denotes the fixed field of the involution of E. As invoked in the proof of Lemma 5.13: if [Λ′,m,m−1,γ_1] and [Λ,m,m−1,γ_2] are self-dual simple strata in A (γ_1, γ_2 skew and minimal over F, with the same minimal polynomial over F) which intertwine in G, then there is g ∈ G with gγ_1g^{−1} = γ_2.

items.name: Intertwining of representations of compact open subgroups (§2, used throughout §6)
items.statement: Setting: C is an algebraically closed field of characteristic ℓ ≠ p. Let 𝒢 be a locally compact topological group, H, H′ compact open subgroups and ρ, ρ′ representations of H, H′ over C. For g ∈ 𝒢, I_g(ρ,ρ′) = Hom_{^gH ∩ H′}(^gρ, ρ′), where ^gH = gHg^{−1} and ^gρ(x) = ρ(g^{−1}xg); I_𝒢(ρ,ρ′) = {g ∈ 𝒢 : I_g(ρ,ρ′) ≠ 0}. g intertwines ρ with ρ′ if I_g(ρ,ρ′) ≠ 0, and ρ intertwines with ρ′ in 𝒢 if I_𝒢(ρ,ρ′) ≠ ∅; for characters (or C = ℂ) the relation is symmetric.
items.note: Defined in §2 (the text writes 'I_g(ρ,ρ′) ≠ ∅' for 'g intertwines', evidently meaning ≠ 0; left to the §2 reader). Missing: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups:SR.0–SR.2 plan smooth representations, Hecke algebras and compact induction but state no intertwining sets; no Mathlib/Tau Ceti declaration (Tau Ceti's intertwining names concern intertwining maps of finite/compact group representations).

Fix a non-trivial character ψ_o : F_o → C^× of conductor p_{F_o}, and define ψ : F → C^× by ψ = ψ_o ∘ T_{F/F_o}.

items.statement: Setting: F is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p (in the paper F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 of such fields), with ring of integers o_F, maximal ideal p_F, residue field k_F and a fixed uniformizer ϖ_F; V is a finite-dimensional F-vector space, A = End_F(V), G̃ = Aut_F(V). items.name: Tame corestriction and derived strata (§6.1)
items.statement: Setting: F is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p (in the paper F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 of such fields), with ring of integers o_F, maximal ideal p_F, residue field k_F and a fixed uniformizer ϖ_F; V is a finite-dimensional F-vector space, A = End_F(V), G̃ = Aut_F(V). items.name: Derived strata are equivalent to simple strata ([39, Theorem 6.14])
items.statement: Setting: F is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p (in the paper F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 of such fields), with ring of integers o_F, maximal ideal p_F, residue field k_F and a fixed uniformizer ϖ_F; V is a finite-dimensional F-vector space, A = End_F(V), G̃ = Aut_F(V). items.name: Self-dual simple characters C^Σ, C_−, H^{r+1}_−, lifts and degree (§6.2)
items.statement: Setting: F/F_o is an extension of degree at most 2 of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p, and x ↦ x̄ generates Gal(F/F_o); ε = ±1 and (V,h) is a finite-dimensional non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (h sesquilinear, linear in the second variable, h(w,v) = ε·conj(h(v,w))); A = End_F(V) with the adjoint anti-involution a ↦ ā of h, A_− = {a ∈ A : ā = −a}; G̃ = Aut_F(V) and G = U(V,h) = {g ∈ G̃ : gḡ = 1}, which is unitary if F ≠ F_o, symplectic if F = F_o and ε = −1, full orthogonal if F = F_o and ε = 1 (the paper's classical group G_o, the connected component, assumed ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o), plays no role here); σ acts on G̃ by σ(g) = ḡ^{−1}. For a self-dual extension (E,β) of F/F_o, E_o denotes the fixed field of the involution of E. C is an algebraically closed field of characteristic ℓ ≠ p (all characters are C-valued); ψ_o : F_o → C^× is the fixed non-trivial character of conductor p_{F_o}, ψ = ψ_o ∘ T_{F/F_o}, and for b ∈ A, ψ_b(x) = ψ(tr_{A/F}(b(x − 1))) (standard Bushnell–Kutzko notation, used but not defined in the paper). Let [Λ,n,r,β] be a self-dual simple stratum in A. Then H^{r+1}(β,Λ) and C(Λ,r,β) are stable under σ, and one defines H^{r+1}_−(β,Λ) = H^{r+1}(β,Λ)^Σ = H^{r+1}(β,Λ) ∩ G (a compact open subgroup of G), C^Σ(Λ,r,β) = {θ ∈ C(Λ,r,β) : θ^σ = θ}, and the set of self-dual simple characters C_−(Λ,r,β) = {θ|_{H^{r+1}_−(β,Λ)} : θ ∈ C^Σ(Λ,r,β)}. For θ_− ∈ C_−(Λ,r,β), its lift (with respect to (Λ,r,β)) is the unique θ ∈ C^Σ(Λ,r,β) with θ|_{H^{r+1}_−(β,Λ)} = θ_−; the degree of θ_− is the degree of its lift (well defined by Propositions 6.2(i) and 6.4).

items.name: G-intertwining implies P_−(Λ)-conjugacy for self-dual simple characters ([39, Theorem 10.3], as invoked)
items.statement: Setting: F/F_o is an extension of degree at most 2 of non-archimedean local fields of odd residual characteristic p, and x ↦ x̄ generates Gal(F/F_o); ε = ±1 and (V,h) is a finite-dimensional non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (h sesquilinear, linear in the second variable, h(w,v) = ε·conj(h(v,w))); A = End_F(V) with the adjoint anti-involution a ↦ ā of h, A_− = {a ∈ A : ā = −a}; G̃ = Aut_F(V) and G = U(V,h) = {g ∈ G̃ : gḡ = 1}, which is unitary if F ≠ F_o, symplectic if F = F_o and ε = −1, full orthogonal if F = F_o and ε = 1 (the paper's classical group G_o, the connected component, assumed ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o), plays no role here); σ acts on G̃ by σ(g) = ḡ^{−1}. items.name: §7.1: simple pair over F
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) A simple pair over F is a pair (k,β) consisting of an element β of some finite field extension of F and an integer k with 0 ≤ k < −k_F(β)·e(F[β]/F), where k_F(β) = k_0(β, 𝔭_E-chain)/e(E/F) (E = F[β]) is the normalised critical exponent of §5.1 (k_0(0,·) = −∞, so (k,0) is a simple pair for every k ≥ 0).

items.name: §7.1: the class Q(k,β) of quadruples and realizations of a simple pair
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) For a simple pair (k,β), E = F[β], Q(k,β) is the class of quadruples (V,ϕ,Λ,r) with (i) V a finite-dimensional F-vector space; (ii) ϕ: E ↪ A = End_F(V) an F-algebra embedding; (iii) Λ an 𝔬_{ϕ(E)}-lattice sequence in V; (iv) r ∈ ℤ with ⌊r/e(Λ|𝔬_{ϕ(E)})⌋ = k. One writes e(Λ|𝔬_E) = e(Λ|𝔬_{ϕ(E)}) and e(Λ) = e(Λ|𝔬_F). For (V,ϕ,Λ,r) ∈ Q(k,β) put n = r if β = 0 and n = −ν_E(β)·e(Λ|𝔬_E) otherwise; the stratum [Λ,n,r,ϕ(β)] in A is called a realization of (k,β).

items.name: §7.1: a realization of a simple pair is a simple stratum (via [12, 1.4.13], [14, 5.1])
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) Let (k,β) be a simple pair and (V,ϕ,Λ,r) ∈ Q(k,β). Then the realization [Λ,n,r,ϕ(β)] is a simple stratum in End_F(V); this follows from k_0(β,Λ) = e(Λ|𝔬_E)·e(E/F)·k_F(β) ([12, 1.4.13], see also [14, 5.1]).

items.name: §7.1: the collection C(k,β) of simple characters of a simple pair
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) For a simple pair (k,β), C(k,β) = ⋃_{(V,ϕ,Λ,r) ∈ Q(k,β)} C(Λ,r,ϕ(β)), the collection of all simple characters (for ψ) defined by realizations of (k,β).

items.name: §7.1: transfer between realizations of a simple pair ([12, 3.6.14], [42, §2.1], [32, §3.1(53)])
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) Given realizations [Λ,n,r,ϕ(β)] (on V) and [Λ',n',r',ϕ'(β)] (on V') of the same simple pair (k,β), there is a canonical bijection τ_{Λ',ϕ',Λ,ϕ,β} = τ_{Λ',Λ,β}: C(Λ,r,ϕ(β)) → C(Λ',r',ϕ'(β)), called transfer; it depends on r, r' (and ϕ, ϕ'), which are suppressed from the notation.

items.name: §7.1: symmetry and transitivity of transfer (recalled)
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) For realizations [Λ,n,r,ϕ(β)], [Λ',n',r',ϕ'(β)], [Λ'',n'',r'',ϕ''(β)] of a simple pair (k,β): τ_{Λ,Λ',β} = τ_{Λ',Λ,β}^{-1} (symmetry) and τ_{Λ'',Λ,β} = τ_{Λ'',Λ',β} ∘ τ_{Λ',Λ,β} (transitivity).

items.name: §7.1: intertwining characterisation of transfer (recalled)
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) Let [Λ,n,r,ϕ(β)] and [Λ',n',r',ϕ'(β)] be realizations of a simple pair (k,β) with ϕ, ϕ': E ↪ End_F(V) on the same space V, and let θ ∈ C(Λ,r,ϕ(β)). Then τ_{Λ',Λ,β}(θ) is the unique θ' ∈ C(Λ',r',ϕ'(β)) such that θ is intertwined with θ' by an element of G̃ = Aut_F(V) which conjugates ϕ to ϕ'. Moreover every element of G̃ which conjugates ϕ to ϕ' intertwines θ with τ_{Λ',Λ,β}(θ).

items.name: §7.1: transfer as restriction through V ⊕ V'
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) Let [Λ,n,r,ϕ(β)] on V and [Λ',n',r',ϕ'(β)] on V' be realizations of a simple pair (k,β) with e(Λ) = e(Λ') (so n' = n). Put V'' = V ⊕ V', ϕ'' = ϕ ⊕ ϕ': E ↪ End_F(V''), Λ'' = Λ ⊕ Λ', r'' = min{r,r'}; then [Λ'',n,r'',ϕ''(β)] is a realization on V''. For θ ∈ C(Λ,r,ϕ(β)) there is a unique θ'' ∈ C(Λ'',r'',ϕ''(β)) such that θ is the restriction of θ'' to H^{r+1}(ϕ''(β),Λ'') ∩ Aut_F(V), and then τ_{Λ',Λ,β}(θ) is the restriction of θ'' to H^{r'+1}(ϕ''(β),Λ'') ∩ Aut_F(V').

items.name: §7.1: potential simple character (ps-character), its realizations and degree
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) A ps-character supported on a simple pair (k,β) is a function Θ: Q(k,β) → C(k,β) such that (i) Θ(V,ϕ,Λ,r) ∈ C(Λ,r,ϕ(β)) for all (V,ϕ,Λ,r) ∈ Q(k,β); (ii) Θ(V',ϕ',Λ',r') = τ_{Λ',Λ,β}(Θ(V,ϕ,Λ,r)) for all (V,ϕ,Λ,r), (V',ϕ',Λ',r') ∈ Q(k,β). The value Θ(V,ϕ,Λ,r) is a realization of Θ; by (ii) Θ is determined by any one of its realizations. The degree is deg(Θ) = [F[β]:F].

items.name: Definition 7.1: endo-equivalence of ps-characters
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) Let Θ, Θ' be ps-characters supported on simple pairs (k,β), (k',β'). They are endo-equivalent, Θ ≈ Θ', if (i) deg(Θ) = deg(Θ'); (ii) k = k'; (iii) there exist a finite-dimensional F-vector space V and quadruples (V,ϕ,Λ,r) ∈ Q(k,β), (V,ϕ',Λ',r') ∈ Q(k',β') such that Θ(V,ϕ,Λ,r) and Θ'(V,ϕ',Λ',r') intertwine in G̃ = Aut_F(V). (This differs mildly from [8, 8.6], [5, 1.10], which exclude ps-characters with trivial realizations.)

items.name: Remark 7.2(i): common realizations in Definition 7.1(iii) may be taken on one strict lattice sequence
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) In Definition 7.1(iii) one may additionally require Λ = Λ' and Λ strict without changing the relation ≈. (Proof: adjust Λ, Λ' in their affine classes to have equal period, apply the †-construction and conjugate by g ∈ G̃^† with gΛ^† = Λ'^†; transfers of intertwining characters intertwine.)

items.name: Remark 7.2(ii): the zero ps-character 0_k is unique and endo-inequivalent to all other ps-characters
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) For every integer k ≥ 0 there is exactly one ps-character supported on (k,0), the zero ps-character 0_k (all its realizations are trivial characters). 0_k is not endo-equivalent to any other ps-character; in particular, if Θ is supported on (k,β) with β ≠ 0 then Θ ≉ 0_k (proof: otherwise F[β] = F and realizations θ ∈ C(Λ,r,β), θ' ∈ C(Λ',r',0) on one space with e(Λ) = e(Λ') intertwine while ⌊r'/e(Λ)⌋ = k < −val_Λ(β)/e(Λ) ∈ ℤ, contradicting Lemma 5.3).

items.name: Remark 7.2(iii): endo-equivalence of ps-characters is an equivalence relation
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) Endo-equivalence ≈ (Definition 7.1) is an equivalence relation on the class of ps-characters (from Remarks 7.2(i),(ii) and [8, Corollary 8.10]).

items.name: External [8, Proposition 8.4] (Bushnell–Henniart): arithmetic invariants of endo-equivalent ps-characters
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) items.name: External [5, Theorem 1.11, 1.13], [8, Corollary 8.7] (Broussous–Sécherre–Stevens, Bushnell–Henniart): realizations of endo-equivalent ps-characters
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) Let Θ ≈ Θ' be non-zero ps-characters supported on (k,β), (k,β'). items.name: Theorem 7.5: all realizations of endo-equivalent ps-characters on a common space intertwine
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) Let Θ, Θ' be endo-equivalent ps-characters supported on simple pairs (k,β), (k,β'), and let θ, θ' be realizations of Θ, Θ' respectively on the same finite-dimensional F-vector space V. Then θ and θ' intertwine in G̃ = Aut_F(V).

items.name: Theorem 7.6(i): transitivity of intertwining for simple characters of equal degree and equal normalised level
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) Let V be a finite-dimensional F-vector space and θ_i ∈ C(Λ_i, r_i, β_i) (i = 1,2,3) simple characters in G̃ = Aut_F(V), E_i = F[β_i]. Suppose θ_1, θ_2 intertwine in G̃ and θ_2, θ_3 intertwine in G̃, that ⌊r_1/e(Λ_1|𝔬_{E_1})⌋ = ⌊r_2/e(Λ_2|𝔬_{E_2})⌋ = ⌊r_3/e(Λ_3|𝔬_{E_3})⌋, and that θ_1, θ_2, θ_3 have the same degree. Then θ_1 and θ_3 intertwine in G̃.

items.name: §7.2: self-dual simple pair, the class Q−(k,β) and self-dual realizations
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V); ε = ±1 fixed; (V,h) an ε-hermitian space over F/F_o, G = U(V,h), and σ the involution of G̃ (and of A) induced by the adjoint anti-involution of h, so G = G̃^σ.) A simple pair (k,β) is self-dual if (E,β), E = F[β], is a self-dual extension of F/F_o (the generator of Gal(F/F_o) extends to an involution x ↦ x̄ of E with β̄ = −β). For such (k,β), Q−(k,β) is the class of ((V,h),ϕ,Λ,r) with (i) (V,h) a finite-dimensional ε-hermitian space over F/F_o; (ii) ϕ: E → A = End_F(V) a self-dual embedding (ϕ(x̄) = ϕ(x)‾ for the adjoint anti-involution of h); (iii) Λ a self-dual 𝔬_{ϕ(E)}-lattice sequence in V; (iv) r ∈ ℤ with ⌊r/e(Λ|𝔬_{ϕ(E)})⌋ = k. Then (V,ϕ,Λ,r) ∈ Q(k,β), and the self-dual simple stratum [Λ,n,r,ϕ(β)] is called a self-dual realization of (k,β).

items.name: External [42, Proposition 2.12] (Stevens): transfer of simple characters commutes with the involutions
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V); ε = ±1 fixed; (V,h) an ε-hermitian space over F/F_o, G = U(V,h), and σ the involution of G̃ (and of A) induced by the adjoint anti-involution of h, so G = G̃^σ.) Let (k,β) be a self-dual simple pair and [Λ,n,r,ϕ(β)], [Λ',n',r',ϕ'(β)] self-dual realizations (on ε-hermitian spaces (V,h), (V',h')). Then the transfer τ_{Λ',Λ,β}: C(Λ,r,ϕ(β)) → C(Λ',r',ϕ'(β)) commutes with the involutions σ, σ' induced by h, h', and restricts (via Glauberman lifts) to a bijection τ_{Λ',Λ,β}: C−(Λ,r,ϕ(β)) → C−(Λ',r',ϕ'(β)).

items.name: §7.2: the collection C−(k,β) of self-dual simple characters of a self-dual simple pair
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V); ε = ±1 fixed; (V,h) an ε-hermitian space over F/F_o, G = U(V,h), and σ the involution of G̃ (and of A) induced by the adjoint anti-involution of h, so G = G̃^σ.) For a self-dual simple pair (k,β), C−(k,β) = ⋃_{((V,h),ϕ,Λ,r) ∈ Q−(k,β)} C−(Λ,r,ϕ(β)), where C−(Λ,r,ϕ(β)) is the set of self-dual simple characters of H^{r+1}_−(ϕ(β),Λ) = H^{r+1}(ϕ(β),Λ) ∩ U(V,h) (§6.2).

items.name: Definition 7.7(i): σ-invariant ps-character
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V); ε = ±1 fixed; (V,h) an ε-hermitian space over F/F_o, G = U(V,h), and σ the involution of G̃ (and of A) induced by the adjoint anti-involution of h, so G = G̃^σ.) Let (k,β) be a self-dual simple pair. A ps-character Θ supported on (k,β) is σ-invariant if, for all ((V,h),ϕ,Λ,r) ∈ Q−(k,β), Θ(V,ϕ,Λ,r) is σ-invariant with respect to (V,h) (i.e. lies in C^Σ(Λ,r,ϕ(β))).

items.name: Definition 7.7(ii): self-dual ps-character and its self-dual realizations
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V); ε = ±1 fixed; (V,h) an ε-hermitian space over F/F_o, G = U(V,h), and σ the involution of G̃ (and of A) induced by the adjoint anti-involution of h, so G = G̃^σ.) Let (k,β) be a self-dual simple pair. A self-dual ps-character supported on (k,β) is a function Θ−: Q−(k,β) → C−(k,β) such that for all ((V,h),ϕ,Λ,r), ((V',h'),ϕ',Λ',r') ∈ Q−(k,β): Θ−((V,h),ϕ,Λ,r) ∈ C−(Λ,r,ϕ(β)) and Θ−((V',h'),ϕ',Λ',r') = τ_{Λ',Λ,β}(Θ−((V,h),ϕ,Λ,r)). Its values are its self-dual realizations; it is determined by any one of them.

items.name: §7.2: every self-dual ps-character has a unique σ-invariant lift (Glauberman)
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V); ε = ±1 fixed; (V,h) an ε-hermitian space over F/F_o, G = U(V,h), and σ the involution of G̃ (and of A) induced by the adjoint anti-involution of h, so G = G̃^σ.) For a self-dual ps-character Θ− supported on a self-dual simple pair (k,β) there is a unique σ-invariant ps-character Θ supported on (k,β) such that Θ(V,ϕ,Λ,r) = Gl(Θ−((V,h),ϕ,Λ,r)) for all ((V,h),ϕ,Λ,r) ∈ Q−(k,β), where Gl is the Glauberman lift C−(Λ,r,ϕ(β)) → C^Σ(Λ,r,ϕ(β)) ⊆ C(Λ,r,ϕ(β)); conversely every self-dual ps-character arises uniquely by restriction from a σ-invariant ps-character. Θ is the lift of Θ−, and deg(Θ−) := deg(Θ) = [F[β]:F].

items.name: External: Glauberman correspondence for self-dual simple/semisimple characters (via [41, §2])
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V); ε = ±1 fixed; (V,h) an ε-hermitian space over F/F_o, G = U(V,h), and σ the involution of G̃ (and of A) induced by the adjoint anti-involution of h, so G = G̃^σ.) For a self-dual simple or semisimple stratum [Λ,n,r,β] (ε-hermitian (V,h)), the group Σ = {1,σ} of order 2 (prime to p) acts on the pro-p group H^{r+1}(β,Λ) and on C(Λ,r,β); restriction θ ↦ θ|_{H^{r+1}_−(β,Λ)} is a bijection C^Σ(Λ,r,β) → C−(Λ,r,β) and coincides with the Glauberman correspondence. The inverse is the (Glauberman) lift.

items.name: Definition 7.8: endo-equivalence of self-dual ps-characters
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V); ε = ±1 fixed; (V,h) an ε-hermitian space over F/F_o, G = U(V,h), and σ the involution of G̃ (and of A) induced by the adjoint anti-involution of h, so G = G̃^σ.) Self-dual ps-characters Θ−, Θ'− supported on self-dual simple pairs (k,β), (k',β') are endo-equivalent, Θ− ≈ Θ'−, if (i) deg(Θ−) = deg(Θ'−); (ii) k = k'; (iii) there exist a finite-dimensional ε-hermitian space (V,h) over F/F_o and ((V,h),ϕ,Λ,r) ∈ Q−(k,β), ((V,h),ϕ',Λ',r') ∈ Q−(k',β') such that Θ−((V,h),ϕ,Λ,r) and Θ'−((V,h),ϕ',Λ',r') intertwine in G = U(V,h).

items.name: Theorem 7.9 (i)–(iv): endo-equivalence of self-dual ps-characters versus their lifts, via concordance
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V); ε = ±1 fixed; (V,h) an ε-hermitian space over F/F_o, G = U(V,h), and σ the involution of G̃ (and of A) induced by the adjoint anti-involution of h, so G = G̃^σ.) Let Θ−, Θ'− be self-dual ps-characters supported on self-dual simple pairs (k,β), (k,β'), with lifts Θ, Θ', and suppose deg(Θ−) = deg(Θ'−). The following are equivalent: (i) Θ ≈ Θ'; (ii) Θ− ≈ Θ'−; (iii) for all ((V,h),ϕ,Λ,r) ∈ Q−(k,β) and ((V,h),ϕ',Λ',r') ∈ Q−(k,β') with (β,ϕ) and (β',ϕ') concordant (Definition 3.25), the realizations Θ−((V,h),ϕ,Λ,r) and Θ'−((V,h),ϕ',Λ',r') intertwine in G = U(V,h); (iv) there exist such quadruples on a common (V,h) with (β,ϕ), (β',ϕ') concordant whose realizations intertwine in G = U(V,h).

items.name: Theorem 7.9 (v): in the non-symplectic case all realizations of endo-equivalent self-dual ps-characters intertwine
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V); ε = ±1 fixed; (V,h) an ε-hermitian space over F/F_o, G = U(V,h), and σ the involution of G̃ (and of A) induced by the adjoint anti-involution of h, so G = G̃^σ.) items.name: Proposition 7.10: realizations of endo-equivalent self-dual ps-characters intertwine iff the embeddings are concordant
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V); ε = ±1 fixed; (V,h) an ε-hermitian space over F/F_o, G = U(V,h), and σ the involution of G̃ (and of A) induced by the adjoint anti-involution of h, so G = G̃^σ.) items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V); ε = ±1 fixed; (V,h) an ε-hermitian space over F/F_o, G = U(V,h), and σ the involution of G̃ (and of A) induced by the adjoint anti-involution of h, so G = G̃^σ.) items.name: §8.1: block notation and splittings of a stratum
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) Let V = ⊕_{i∈I} V^i be a decomposition into F-subspaces. For J ⊆ I put V^J = ⊕_{i∈J} V^i, e^J: V → V^J the projection with kernel ⊕_{j∈I∖J} V^j, A^J = End_F(V^J), G̃^J = Aut_F(V^J) (A^i, G̃^i for J = {i}). For a stratum [Λ,n,r,β] in A put Λ^J = Λ ∩ V^J, β_J = e^J β e^J and n_J = max{−val_{Λ^J}(β_J), r}, so [Λ^J,n_J,r,β_J] is a stratum in A^J. The decomposition is a splitting of [Λ,n,r,β] if β = Σ_{i∈I} β_i and Λ(k) = ⊕_{i∈I} Λ^i(k) for all k ∈ ℤ.

items.name: Definition 8.1: semisimple stratum (and E = ⊕E_i, B_β, G̃_β, degree)
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) A stratum [Λ,n,r,β] in A is semisimple if it is null, or val_Λ(β) = −n and there is a splitting V = ⊕_{i∈I} V^i of it such that (i) for each i ∈ I the stratum [Λ^i,n_i,r,β_i] in End_F(V^i) is simple; (ii) for i ≠ j the stratum [Λ^{{i,j}}, n_{{i,j}}, r, β_{{i,j}}] is not equivalent to a simple stratum in End_F(V^{{i,j}}). Then E = F[β] = ⊕_{i∈I} E_i with E_i = F[β_i] fields, B_β = C_A(β), G̃_β = B_β^×; an 𝔬_F-lattice sequence which is a sum of 𝔬_{E_i}-lattice sequences in the V^i is called an 𝔬_E-lattice sequence (so Λ is one), and [E:F] = dim_F E is the degree of the stratum.

items.name: §8.1: critical exponent k_0(β,Λ) and k_F(β) of a semisimple stratum
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) For a non-null semisimple stratum [Λ,n,0,β], k_0(β,Λ) = −min{r ∈ ℤ : r ≥ 0, [Λ,n,r,β] is not semisimple} (the critical exponent) and k_F(β) = k_0(β,Λ)/e(Λ), which is independent of Λ ([42, §3.1]). For null strata k_0(0,Λ) = k_F(0) = −∞.

items.name: Lemma 8.2: large inverse powers of a uniformiser make a split element semisimple
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) Let β ∈ A generate a commutative semisimple algebra E = F[β] = ⊕_{i∈I} E_i (a product of fields), let Λ be an 𝔬_E-lattice sequence in V, n = −val_Λ(β) and e = e(Λ). If β ≠ 0 then for every sufficiently large integer l the stratum [Λ, n+le, 0, ϖ_F^{−l}β] is semisimple.

items.name: §8.1: σ-action on the index set of a self-dual semisimple stratum; I_0, I_+, I_−
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V); ε = ±1 fixed; (V,h) an ε-hermitian space over F/F_o, G = U(V,h), and σ the involution of G̃ (and of A) induced by the adjoint anti-involution of h, so G = G̃^σ.) Let [Λ,n,r,β] be self-dual (Λ self-dual, β ∈ A_−) and semisimple with splitting V = ⊕_{i∈I} V^i. For each i ∈ I there is a unique σ(i) = j ∈ I with β̄_i = −β_j (bar = adjoint anti-involution of h). Put I_0 = {i ∈ I : σ(i) = i}, choose representatives I_+ of the σ-orbits in I∖I_0 and put I_− = σ(I_+), so I = I_+ ⊔ I_0 ⊔ I_−. For σ-stable J ⊆ I, h_J = h|_{V^J} and (V^J,h_J) is an ε-hermitian space over F/F_o.

items.name: Definition 8.3: skew semisimple stratum
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V); ε = ±1 fixed; (V,h) an ε-hermitian space over F/F_o, G = U(V,h), and σ the involution of G̃ (and of A) induced by the adjoint anti-involution of h, so G = G̃^σ.) items.name: Proposition 8.4 ([42, Proposition 3.4], [29, Lemma 3.1]): split semisimple approximation
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V); ε = ±1 fixed; (V,h) an ε-hermitian space over F/F_o, G = U(V,h), and σ the involution of G̃ (and of A) induced by the adjoint anti-involution of h, so G = G̃^σ.) Let [Λ,n,0,β] be a non-null semisimple stratum with associated splitting ⊕_{i∈I} V^i and let 0 < r ≤ n. Then there is a semisimple stratum [Λ,n,r,γ] equivalent to [Λ,n,r,β] with γ ∈ ⊕_{i∈I} A^i. If [Λ,n,0,β] is self-dual then [Λ,n,r,γ] may be taken self-dual.

items.name: §8.2: the groups H^m(β,Λ) and semisimple characters C(Λ,r,β) ([42, §3.2]); block restrictions
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) To a semisimple stratum [Λ,n,r,β] in A are attached an 𝔬_F-order H(β,Λ) in A (defined inductively, [42, Section 3.2]), the compact open subgroups H^m(β,Λ) = H(β,Λ) ∩ P_m(Λ) (m ≥ 1) of G̃, and a set C(Λ,r,β) of characters of H^{r+1}(β,Λ), the semisimple characters (depending on ψ). For J ⊆ I there is a natural embedding H^{r+1}(β_J,Λ^J) ↪ H^{r+1}(β,Λ), hence a restriction map C(Λ,r,β) → C(Λ^J,r,β_J), θ ↦ θ_J; θ_i (J = {i}) is a simple block restriction.

items.name: External [42, Lemma 3.15]: Iwahori decomposition of semisimple characters
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) If P̃ is a parabolic subgroup of G̃ with Levi factor M̃ stabilising a decomposition of V which splits a semisimple stratum [Λ,n,r,β] (e.g. its splitting), with unipotent radical Ũ and opposite Ũ^−, then H^{r+1}(β,Λ) has an Iwahori decomposition with respect to (M̃,P̃) and every θ ∈ C(Λ,r,β) is trivial on H^{r+1}(β,Λ) ∩ Ũ and H^{r+1}(β,Λ) ∩ Ũ^−; so θ is determined by θ|_{H^{r+1}(β,Λ) ∩ M̃} = ⊗_i θ_i.

items.name: §8.2: e(Λ_E) and transfer of semisimple characters on a common space ([42, Prop. 3.26], [43, Rem. 3.3])
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) For a semisimple stratum with splitting ⊕V^i, e(Λ_E) = gcd_{i∈I} e(Λ^i|𝔬_{E_i}). Given semisimple strata [Λ,n,r,β] and [Λ',n',r',β] in A with ⌊r/e(Λ_E)⌋ = ⌊r'/e(Λ'_E)⌋ there is a canonical bijection τ_{Λ',Λ,β}: C(Λ,r,β) → C(Λ',r',β): for θ ∈ C(Λ,r,β), τ_{Λ',Λ,β}(θ) is the unique θ' ∈ C(Λ',r',β) such that 1 ∈ G̃ intertwines θ with θ'.

items.name: §8.2: self-dual semisimple characters C−(Λ,r,β) and their lifts
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V); ε = ±1 fixed; (V,h) an ε-hermitian space over F/F_o, G = U(V,h), and σ the involution of G̃ (and of A) induced by the adjoint anti-involution of h, so G = G̃^σ.) Let [Λ,n,r,β] be a self-dual semisimple stratum. H^{r+1}(β,Λ) and C(Λ,r,β) are σ-stable ([42, §3.6], [29, §3.6]); put H^{r+1}_−(β,Λ) = H^{r+1}(β,Λ)^Σ = H^{r+1}(β,Λ) ∩ G (compact open in G), C^Σ(Λ,r,β) = {θ ∈ C(Λ,r,β) : θ^σ = θ} and C−(Λ,r,β) = {θ|_{H^{r+1}_−(β,Λ)} : θ ∈ C^Σ(Λ,r,β)} (self-dual semisimple characters). Restriction is the Glauberman correspondence, so each θ− ∈ C−(Λ,r,β) has a unique lift θ ∈ C^Σ(Λ,r,β) with θ|_{H^{r+1}_−(β,Λ)} = θ−.

items.name: Definition 8.5: matching of semisimple characters
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) Let [Λ,n,r,β], [Λ',n',r',β'] be semisimple strata in A with splittings V = ⊕_{i∈I} V^i and V = ⊕_{i∈I'} V'^i, and θ ∈ C(Λ,r,β), θ' ∈ C(Λ',r',β'). If ζ: I → I' is a bijection and g ∈ Aut_F(V) satisfies, for each i ∈ I, (i) gV^i = V'^{ζ(i)} and (ii) ^gθ_i and θ'_{ζ(i)} intertwine in Aut_F(V'^{ζ(i)}), then ζ is a matching from (θ,β) to (θ',β'), and θ intertwines θ' in Aut_F(V) with matching ζ.

items.name: Proposition 8.6: intertwining with a prescribed matching is blockwise (8.7)
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) Let θ ∈ C(Λ,r,β), θ' ∈ C(Λ',r',β') be semisimple characters in G̃ and ζ: I → I' a bijection of their index sets. For i ∈ I let I(θ_i,θ'_{ζ(i)}) be the set of isomorphisms g ∈ Hom_F(V^i, V'^{ζ(i)}) such that ^gθ_i is intertwined with θ'_{ζ(i)} by the identity. Then I_G̃(θ,θ') ∩ ∏_{i∈I} Hom_F(V^i, V'^{ζ(i)}) = ∏_{i∈I} I(θ_i, θ'_{ζ(i)}).

items.name: Theorem 8.8 ([39, Theorem 10.1]): the Matching Theorem
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) Let [Λ,n,r,β], [Λ',n',r,β'] be semisimple strata in A with e(Λ) = e(Λ') and splittings indexed by I, I', and let θ ∈ C(Λ,r,β), θ' ∈ C(Λ',r,β') be semisimple characters which intertwine in G̃. Then there is a unique matching ζ: I → I' from (θ,β) to (θ',β'). Moreover, if g ∈ G̃ satisfies gV^i = V'^{ζ(i)} for all i ∈ I, then ^gθ_i and θ'_{ζ(i)} intertwine in Aut_F(V'^{ζ(i)}).

items.name: Corollary 8.11: for transferred characters the matching respects characteristic polynomials
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) items.name: Remark 8.12: example — without the transfer hypothesis Corollary 8.11 fails (char F = p)
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) items.name: §8.3: the normalising subgroup S_r(β,Λ) ([42, §3.2] Γ_r(β,Λ); [39, Prop. 9.8]; [12, (3.5.1)])
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) items.name: (8.14): the lattice-quotient condition on a matching
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) items.name: Corollary 8.19 (main part): intertwining self-dual semisimple characters admit defining elements with matched characteristic polynomials
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V); ε = ±1 fixed; (V,h) an ε-hermitian space over F/F_o, G = U(V,h), and σ the involution of G̃ (and of A) induced by the adjoint anti-involution of h, so G = G̃^σ.) Let [Λ,n,r,β], [Λ',n,r,β'] be self-dual semisimple strata with e(Λ) = e(Λ') and splittings ⊕_{i∈I} V^i, ⊕_{i∈I'} V'^i; let θ− ∈ C−(Λ,r,β), θ'− ∈ C−(Λ',r,β') intertwine by an element of G, with matching ζ: I → I'. Then there exist self-dual semisimple strata [Λ,n,r,β̃] and [Λ',n,r,β̃'] with splittings V = ⊕_{i∈I} V^i and V = ⊕_{i∈I'} V'^i such that C(Λ,r,β) = C(Λ,r,β̃), C(Λ',r,β') = C(Λ',r,β̃') and, for all i ∈ I, β̃_i and β̃'_{ζ(i)} have the same characteristic polynomial. (Corrected statement; the printed one has Λ and Λ' interchanged — see sourceIssues.)

items.name: External [39, Theorems 6.15, 6.16] (Skodlerack–Stevens): semisimple and simple representatives of split strata
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V); ε = ±1 fixed; (V,h) an ε-hermitian space over F/F_o, G = U(V,h), and σ the involution of G̃ (and of A) induced by the adjoint anti-involution of h, so G = G̃^σ.) (As used.) (6.15) A (self-dual) stratum split by a decomposition, e.g. a derived stratum [Λ,r+1,r,s_γ(·)] or [Λ,n,r,β+c], is equivalent to a (self-dual) semisimple stratum whose splitting is a coarsening of the given decomposition. (6.16) If a stratum split by a decomposition V = ⊕V^i is equivalent to a simple stratum, it is equivalent to a simple stratum split by the same decomposition, which can be taken self-dual if the stratum is self-dual.

items.name: Standard input: hyperbolic ε-hermitian spaces of equal dimension are isometric; Witt cancellation
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V); ε = ±1 fixed; (V,h) an ε-hermitian space over F/F_o, G = U(V,h), and σ the involution of G̃ (and of A) induced by the adjoint anti-involution of h, so G = G̃^σ.) Two hyperbolic ε-hermitian spaces over F/F_o of the same F-dimension are isometric; and (Witt cancellation) if (V_1,h_1) ⊥ (W,k) ≅ (V_2,h_2) ⊥ (W',k') with (W,k) ≅ (W',k') non-degenerate, then (V_1,h_1) ≅ (V_2,h_2).

items.name: Definition 9.1: semisimple pair, index set, component simple pairs, (k_J,β_J)
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) A semisimple pair is (k,β) with β an element of a finite-dimensional commutative semisimple F-algebra, E = F[β] = ⊕_{i∈I} E_i (E_i fields), and k ∈ ℤ with 0 ≤ k/e_E < −k_F(β), where e_E = lcm_{i∈I} e_i, e_i = e(E_i/F), and k_F(β) is the generalised critical exponent (after Lemma 8.2). I is the index set of (k,β). Writing β = Σ_{i∈I} β_i and k_i = ⌊k e_i/e_E⌋, the (k_i,β_i) are the component simple pairs. For non-empty J ⊆ I put β_J = Σ_{j∈J} β_j, e_J = lcm_{j∈J} e_j, k_J = ⌊k e_J/e_E⌋.

items.name: §9.1: components and sub-sums of a semisimple pair are (semi)simple pairs
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) For a semisimple pair (k,β) with index set I: each (k_i,β_i) (k_i = ⌊k e_i/e_E⌋) is a simple pair, because k_F(β_i) ≤ k_F(β); and for every non-empty J ⊆ I, (k_J,β_J) is a semisimple pair.

items.name: §9.1: self-dual semisimple pair; the σ-action on the index set; I_0, I_+, I_−
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V); ε = ±1 fixed; (V,h) an ε-hermitian space over F/F_o, G = U(V,h), and σ the involution of G̃ (and of A) induced by the adjoint anti-involution of h, so G = G̃^σ.) A semisimple pair (k,β) is self-dual if the involution x ↦ x̄ of F extends to an involution of E = F[β] with β̄ = −β. Writing the minimal polynomial of β as Ψ(X) = ∏_{i∈I} Ψ_i(X) with Ψ_i irreducible (E_i ≅ F[X]/(Ψ_i)), the action of x ↦ x̄ on the primitive idempotents of E defines an involution σ of I; I_0 = {i : σ(i) = i}, I_+ is a set of representatives of the σ-orbits in I∖I_0 and I_− = σ(I_+), so I = I_+ ⊔ I_0 ⊔ I_−.

items.name: §9.1: Q(k,β), realizations and C(k,β) for a semisimple pair
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) For a semisimple pair (k,β), Q(k,β) is the class of (V,ϕ,Λ,r) with (i) V a finite-dimensional F-vector space; (ii) ϕ: E ↪ A = End_F(V) an embedding; (iii) Λ an 𝔬_{ϕ(E)}-lattice sequence in V; (iv) r ∈ ℤ with ⌊r/e(Λ_E)⌋ = k, where e(Λ_E) = e(Λ|𝔬_F)/e_E = gcd_{i∈I} e(Λ^i|𝔬_{ϕ(E_i)}). For (V,ϕ,Λ,r) ∈ Q(k,β), with n = max{r, −val_Λ(ϕ(β))}, [Λ,n,r,ϕ(β)] is a semisimple stratum with splitting V = ⊕_{i∈I} V^i, V^i = ker Ψ_i(ϕ(β)) (all non-zero), called a realization of (k,β); C(k,β) = ⋃_{(V,ϕ,Λ,r) ∈ Q(k,β)} C(Λ,r,ϕ(β)).

items.name: §9.1: self-dual embeddings, Q−(k,β), self-dual realizations and C−(k,β) for a self-dual semisimple pair
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V); ε = ±1 fixed; (V,h) an ε-hermitian space over F/F_o, G = U(V,h), and σ the involution of G̃ (and of A) induced by the adjoint anti-involution of h, so G = G̃^σ.) Let (k,β) be a self-dual semisimple pair. For an ε-hermitian space (V,h) over F/F_o, an embedding ϕ: E ↪ A = End_F(V) is self-dual if ϕ(x̄) = ϕ(x)‾ for all x ∈ E (bar on A the adjoint anti-involution of h). Q−(k,β) is the class of ((V,h),ϕ,Λ,r) with (V,h) finite-dimensional ε-hermitian over F/F_o, (V,ϕ,Λ,r) ∈ Q(k,β), and ϕ, Λ self-dual; the realization [Λ,n,r,ϕ(β)] is then a self-dual semisimple stratum (a self-dual realization), and C−(k,β) = ⋃_{((V,h),ϕ,Λ,r) ∈ Q−(k,β)} C−(Λ,r,ϕ(β)).

items.name: Lemma 9.3 and the transfer of semisimple characters between realizations of a semisimple pair
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) Let (k,β) be a semisimple pair with index set I, (V,ϕ,Λ,r), (V',ϕ',Λ',r') ∈ Q(k,β), θ ∈ C(Λ,r,ϕ(β)), and M̃ ⊆ G̃ = Aut_F(V) the Levi subgroup of V = ⊕_{i∈I} V^i, so θ|_{H^{r+1}(ϕ(β),Λ) ∩ M̃} = ⊗_{i∈I} θ_i with θ_i ∈ C(Λ^i,r,ϕ(β_i)). Put θ'_i = τ_{Λ'^i,Λ^i,β_i}(θ_i) (transfer for the component simple pair (k_i,β_i)) and let M̃' ⊆ Aut_F(V') be the stabiliser of V' = ⊕_{i∈I} V'^i. Then there is a unique semisimple character θ' ∈ C(Λ',r',ϕ'(β)) with θ'|_{H^{r'+1}(ϕ'(β),Λ') ∩ M̃'} = ⊗_{i∈I} θ'_i. Setting τ_{Λ',Λ,β}(θ) = θ' defines a bijection τ_{Λ',Λ,β}: C(Λ,r,ϕ(β)) → C(Λ',r',ϕ'(β)) (transfer).

items.name: §9.2: transfer between self-dual realizations commutes with σ (as in [42, Proposition 3.32])
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V); ε = ±1 fixed; (V,h) an ε-hermitian space over F/F_o, G = U(V,h), and σ the involution of G̃ (and of A) induced by the adjoint anti-involution of h, so G = G̃^σ.) Let (k,β) be a self-dual semisimple pair and [Λ,n,r,ϕ(β)], [Λ',n',r',ϕ'(β)] self-dual realizations (on (V,h), (V',h')). Then τ_{Λ',Λ,β} commutes with the actions of the adjoint anti-involutions of h and h' on C(Λ,r,ϕ(β)), C(Λ',r',ϕ'(β)), and restricts to a bijection τ_{Λ',Λ,β}: C−(Λ,r,ϕ(β)) → C−(Λ',r',ϕ'(β)).

items.name: Definition 9.4: potential semisimple character (pss-character), realizations and degree
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) A pss-character supported on a semisimple pair (k,β) is a function Θ: Q(k,β) → C(k,β) such that (i) Θ(V,ϕ,Λ,r) ∈ C(Λ,r,ϕ(β)) for all (V,ϕ,Λ,r) ∈ Q(k,β); (ii) Θ(V',ϕ',Λ',r') = τ_{Λ',Λ,β}(Θ(V,ϕ,Λ,r)) for all pairs of elements of Q(k,β). Its values are its realizations (Θ is determined by any one); deg(Θ) = [F[β]:F].

items.name: Definition 9.5(i): σ-invariant pss-character
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V); ε = ±1 fixed; (V,h) an ε-hermitian space over F/F_o, G = U(V,h), and σ the involution of G̃ (and of A) induced by the adjoint anti-involution of h, so G = G̃^σ.) items.name: Definition 9.5(ii): self-dual pss-character and its self-dual realizations

items.name: §9.3: every self-dual pss-character has a unique σ-invariant lift (Glauberman)
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V); ε = ±1 fixed; (V,h) an ε-hermitian space over F/F_o, G = U(V,h), and σ the involution of G̃ (and of A) induced by the adjoint anti-involution of h, so G = G̃^σ.) For a self-dual pss-character Θ− supported on a self-dual semisimple pair (k,β) there is a unique σ-invariant pss-character Θ supported on (k,β) with Θ(V,ϕ,Λ,r) = Gl(Θ−((V,h),ϕ,Λ,r)) (Glauberman lift in C(Λ,r,ϕ(β))) for all ((V,h),ϕ,Λ,r) ∈ Q−(k,β); every self-dual pss-character arises uniquely by restriction from a σ-invariant pss-character. Θ is the lift of Θ−, and deg(Θ−) := deg(Θ) = [F[β]:F].

items.name: §9.3: Levi decomposition of self-dual semisimple characters ([43, Propositions 5.4, 5.5], [3, 4.3 Lemma 1])
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V); ε = ±1 fixed; (V,h) an ε-hermitian space over F/F_o, G = U(V,h), and σ the involution of G̃ (and of A) induced by the adjoint anti-involution of h, so G = G̃^σ.) Let [Λ,n,r,β] be a self-dual semisimple stratum with index set I = I_+ ⊔ I_0 ⊔ I_−, so V = ⊕_{i∈I_+}(V^i ⊕ V^{σ(i)}) ⊕ ⊕_{i∈I_0} V^i, and let M = M̃ ∩ G be the stabiliser in G of this decomposition (M̃ the corresponding Levi subgroup of G̃). Then H^{r+1}_−(β,Λ) ∩ M ≅ ∏_{i∈I_+} H^{r+1}(β_i,Λ^i) × ∏_{i∈I_0} H^{r+1}_−(β_i,Λ^i), and for θ ∈ C−(Λ,r,β) (with lift having simple block restrictions θ_i) one has θ|_{H^{r+1}_−(β,Λ) ∩ M} = ⊗_{i∈I_+} θ_i^2 ⊗ ⊗_{i∈I_0} θ_{i,−}, with θ_i ∈ C(Λ^i,r,β_i) (i ∈ I_+) and θ_{i,−} ∈ C−(Λ^i,r,β_i) (i ∈ I_0). Moreover, for i ∈ I_+, H^{r+1}(β_i,Λ^i) = H^{r+1}(2β_i,Λ^i) and θ_i^2 ∈ C(Λ^i,r,2β_i).

items.name: Lemma 9.6(i): restriction of pss-characters to sub-sums
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) items.name: Lemma 9.6(ii): the component ps-characters of a pss-character are pairwise endo-inequivalent
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) items.name: Definition 9.8: endo-equivalence of pss-characters

items.name: Theorem 9.9(i): endo-equivalence of pss-characters is componentwise, with a unique matching
items.statement: (Standing: F_o a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F = F_o or F/F_o quadratic, x ↦ x̄ the generator of Gal(F/F_o); C algebraically closed of characteristic ≠ p, all characters C^×-valued; ψ = ψ_o∘Tr_{F/F_o} with ψ_o: F_o → C^× non-trivial of conductor 𝔭_{F_o}; for a finite-dimensional F-vector space V, A = End_F(V) and G̃ = Aut_F(V).) Let Θ, Θ' be pss-characters supported on semisimple pairs (k,β), (k,β') with index sets I, I'. items.name: Lemma 10.1: G°- versus G∖G°-intertwining detected by determinants of symplectic isometries
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) In §10, ε = 1 and F = F_o, so G = O(V, h) is orthogonal and G° = SO(V, h). For a ∈ A, a*(h) denotes the twisted form (v, w) ↦ h(v, aw). Let [Λ, n, r, β] and [Λ′, n, r, β′] be self-dual semisimple strata in A, with associated splittings V = ⊕_{i∈I} V^i and V = ⊕_{i∈I′} V′^i, and suppose β ≠ 0 and β′ ≠ 0. Let θ₋ ∈ C₋(Λ, r, β) and θ′₋ ∈ C₋(Λ′, r, β′) be self-dual semisimple characters which intertwine in G, and suppose β normalizes Λ. Then θ₋ and θ′₋ intertwine in G° (respectively in G ∖ G°) if and only if the symplectic spaces (V, β*(h)) and (V, β′*(h)) are isometric by an automorphism of V of determinant congruent to 1 modulo p_F (respectively to −1 modulo p_F).

items.name: Theorem 10.2(ii): without zero component, G°-intertwining iff determinant-1 isometry of the twisted symplectic forms
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) In §10, ε = 1 and F = F_o, so G = O(V, h) is orthogonal and G° = SO(V, h). For a ∈ A, a*(h) denotes the twisted form (v, w) ↦ h(v, aw). Let θ₋ ∈ C₋(Λ, r, β) and θ′₋ ∈ C₋(Λ′, r, β′) be self-dual semisimple characters which intertwine in G. If β has no zero component, then θ₋ and θ′₋ intertwine under an element of G° if and only if (V, β*(h)) and (V, β′*(h)) are isometric by an automorphism of V of determinant congruent to 1 modulo p_F; in this case every element of G intertwining θ₋ and θ′₋ is in G°. Equivalently, they intertwine under an element of G ∖ G° if and only if these symplectic spaces are isometric by an automorphism of determinant congruent to −1 modulo p_F, in which case every element of G intertwining θ₋ and θ′₋ lies in G ∖ G°.

items.name: Example (§10.2, corrected by E48): G°-intertwining and G-conjugate but not G°-conjugate self-dual semisimple characters
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) In §10, ε = 1 and F = F_o, so G = O(V, h) is orthogonal and G° = SO(V, h). For a ∈ A, a*(h) denotes the twisted form (v, w) ↦ h(v, aw). Let [Λ, n, r, β] be a self-dual semisimple stratum in A with associated splitting V = ⊕_{i∈I} V^i and let θ ∈ C^Σ(Λ, r, β). Suppose there exists i₀ ∈ I with β_{i₀} = 0 such that P₋(Λ^{i₀}) has no element of determinant −1 in its normalizer. Take g_{i₀} ∈ U(V^{i₀}, h_{i₀}) of determinant −1, g_i = id for i ≠ i₀, g = Σ_i g_i, and θ′ = ^gθ. Then θ and θ′ intertwine by an element of G° (Theorem 10.2) but are not conjugate by an element of G°, provided r = 0 or, for r ≥ 1, the normalizer of P^{r+1}₋(Λ^{i₀}) in U(V^{i₀}, h_{i₀}) contains no element of determinant −1. (The paper assumes only the condition on P₋(Λ^{i₀}), which does not suffice for r ≥ 1; see E48.)

Suppose that e(Λ) = e(Λ′), let [Λ, n, r, β] and [Λ′, n, r, β′] be self-dual semisimple strata in A with splittings V = ⊕_{i∈I} V^i and V = ⊕_{i∈I′} V′^i, and let θ ∈ C₋(Λ, r, β) and θ′ ∈ C₋(Λ′, r, β′) be self-dual semisimple characters which intertwine in G° with matching ζ : I → I′. items.name: Fact: every isometry of a symplectic space has determinant 1
items.statement: Let (W, ω) be a finite-dimensional symplectic space over a field F (ω non-degenerate alternating). Every F-linear isometry of (W, ω) has determinant 1; consequently all isometries between two symplectic forms on the same space have the same determinant.
items.locator: used in Lemma 10.1 (p. 57), Theorem 10.2(ii) (p. 57), Lemma 12.32 (p. 74), arXiv:1611.02667v3
items.note: Near-library: mathlib:SymplecticGroup.det_eq_one proves det M = 1 for every M with M J Mᵀ = J (Matrix.symplecticGroup, standard J, any commutative ring) — read and confirmed. The coordinate-free statement needs a symplectic (Darboux) basis for an arbitrary non-degenerate alternating form, which neither Mathlib nor Tau Ceti states (tauceti:LinearMap.IsAlt.compl₁₂_self_eq_det_smul covers rank 2 only). Marked missing to be conservative; the gap is a short transport.

items.name: (11.1): reductive quotient of P₋(Λ_E) and the parahoric P°₋(Λ_E)
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) In §11, G° has compact centre (G is not F-isomorphic to O(1,1)(F)) and representations are smooth representations on C-vector spaces. Let [Λ, n, 0, β] be a skew semisimple stratum with index set I = I₀, E = F[β] = ⊕_{i∈I} E_i, and b_n = b_n(Λ) = a_n(Λ) ∩ B_β = ⊕_i b_n^i. Then P₋(Λ_E)/P¹₋(Λ_E) is the set of rational points of the reductive group ∏_{i∈I} Res_{k_{E_i,o}|k_o}(U(ī)) defined over k_o, where U(ī) is the reductive group defined by the anti-involution restricted to b⁰_i/b¹_i and Res is Weil restriction; the parahoric subgroup P°₋(Λ_E) is the preimage of the k_o-rational points of the neutral component of this group.

items.name: Lemma 11.4: a finite classical group abstractly isomorphic to O(1,1)(k) is O(1,1)
items.statement: Let k be a finite field of odd characteristic p, with an involution x ↦ x̄ on k with fixed field k_o. Let H be an algebraic group defined over k_o and k_o-isomorphic to a symplectic, a unitary or an orthogonal group over k_o. Suppose H(k_o) is isomorphic to O(1,1)(k) as an abstract group. Then k = k_o and H is k-isomorphic to O(1,1).

items.name: Definition 11.6: cuspidal type for G°
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) In §11, G° has compact centre (G is not F-isomorphic to O(1,1)(F)) and representations are smooth representations on C-vector spaces. A cuspidal type for G° is a pair (J, λ) such that there exist a cuspidal skew semisimple stratum [Λ, n, 0, β] and θ₋ ∈ C₋(Λ, 0, β) with J = J₋(β, Λ) and λ = κ ⊗ τ, where κ is a β-extension of the unique irreducible representation of J¹₋(β, Λ) containing θ₋, and τ is an irreducible representation of J₋(β, Λ)/J¹₋(β, Λ) whose restriction to J°₋(β, Λ)/J¹₋(β, Λ) is cuspidal.

items.name: Proposition 11.7: a cuspidal type is insensitive to changing β within C(Λ, 0, β)
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) Let (J, λ) be a cuspidal type for G° defined via a cuspidal stratum [Λ, n, 0, β], with λ = κ ⊗ τ. Suppose [Λ, n, 0, β′] is a skew semisimple stratum with C(Λ, 0, β) = C(Λ, 0, β′). items.name: Mackey consequence: conjugate types give isomorphic inductions; isomorphic inductions force intertwining
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) In §11, G° has compact centre (G is not F-isomorphic to O(1,1)(F)) and representations are smooth representations on C-vector spaces. If cuspidal types (J, λ) and (J′, λ′) for G° are G°-conjugate then ind_J^{G°} λ ≅ ind_{J′}^{G°} λ′; conversely, if ind_J^{G°} λ ≅ ind_{J′}^{G°} λ′ then (J, λ) and (J′, λ′) intertwine in G°.
