items.name: Theorem 11.9 (classification form, §1.4): isomorphism of cuspidal representations iff G°-conjugacy of types
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) items.name: Lemma 12.4: extending a semisimple character one step with prescribed block restriction
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p (a finite extension of F_o as in §2); V a finite-dimensional F-vector space, G̃ = GL_F(V) = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) Let [Λ, n, r, β] and [Λ, n, r+1, γ̃] be semisimple strata split by V = V¹ ⊕ V² such that [Λ, n, r+1, β] is equivalent to [Λ, n, r+1, γ̃]. Put Λ¹ = Λ ∩ V¹, β¹ = β|_{V¹}, and similarly Λ², β². Given θ̃ ∈ C(Λ, r+1, γ̃) and an extension θ¹ ∈ C(Λ¹, r, β¹) of θ̃|_{H^{r+2}(β¹,Λ¹)}, there is a semisimple character θ ∈ C(Λ, r, β) whose restriction to H^{r+1}(β¹, Λ¹) is θ¹ and whose restriction to H^{r+2}(β, Λ) is θ̃.

items.name: Lemma 12.6: adjusting a simple block so that a direct sum becomes semisimple
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p (a finite extension of F_o as in §2); V a finite-dimensional F-vector space, G̃ = GL_F(V) = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) items.name: Lemma 12.7: gluing two semisimple characters on V¹ and V²
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p (a finite extension of F_o as in §2); V a finite-dimensional F-vector space, G̃ = GL_F(V) = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) items.name: Degree of a full simple character and of a simple endo-class
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p (a finite extension of F_o as in §2); V a finite-dimensional F-vector space, G̃ = GL_F(V) = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) The degree of a full simple character θ ∈ C(Λ, 0, β) is [F[β] : F]; it is invariant under intertwining of full simple characters and under transfer. The degree deg(c) of a simple endo-class c ∈ E is the common degree of the values of the ps-characters in c.

items.name: Definition 12.8: endo-parameter for G̃ and its degree
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p (a finite extension of F_o as in §2); V a finite-dimensional F-vector space, G̃ = GL_F(V) = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) An endo-parameter is a function f : E → ℕ₀ with finite support. Its degree is deg(f) := Σ_{c∈E} deg(c) f(c).

items.name: The endo-parameter f_θ of a full semisimple character
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p (a finite extension of F_o as in §2); V a finite-dimensional F-vector space, G̃ = GL_F(V) = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) Given a full semisimple character θ ∈ C(Λ, 0, β), let Θ be the pss-character supported on (0, β) with Θ(V, ϕ_β, Λ, 0) = θ (ϕ_β the canonical embedding of F[β]) and c_i (i ∈ I) the endo-classes of its simple block restrictions. Then f_θ is the endo-parameter with support F([Θ]) and f_θ(c_i) := dim_F V^i / deg(c_i), i ∈ I.

items.name: Theorem 12.9: endo-parameters classify intertwining classes of full semisimple characters of GL_F(V)
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p (a finite extension of F_o as in §2); V a finite-dimensional F-vector space, G̃ = GL_F(V) = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) There is a canonical bijection from the set of G̃-intertwining classes of full semisimple characters for G̃ = GL_F(V) to the set of endo-parameters f of degree dim_F(V), defined by mapping the intertwining class of a full semisimple character θ to f_θ.

items.name: Definition 12.10: the ps-character Θ^f
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) Fix an algebraic closure F^alg of F, an automorphism f of F^alg extending x ↦ x̄ on F, and a sign ε. Let Ps(F^alg) be the set of full ps-characters supported on simple pairs (0, β) with F[β] ⊆ F^alg. Given Θ ∈ Ps(F^alg) supported on (0, β), put E = F[β] and choose: a finite-dimensional F-vector space V with [E:F] | dim_F V; an F-linear field embedding ϕ : E → A = End_F(V); a hyperbolic ε-hermitian space (V_h, h) over F/F_o with complete polarization V_h = V ⊕ V^#; an o_E-lattice sequence Λ in V. Then (0, −f(β)) is a simple pair; set E^# = f(E), Λ^#(r) = {v ∈ V^# | h(v, Λ(1 − r)) ⊆ p_F}, and ϕ^# : E^# ↪ End_F(V^#), ϕ^#(x) = \overline{ϕ(f⁻¹(x))} (adjoint anti-involution of V_h). Then (V^#, ϕ^#, Λ^#, 0) ∈ Q(0, −f(β)), and Θ^f is the unique full ps-character supported on (0, −f(β)) with Θ^f(V^#, ϕ^#, Λ^#, 0)(y) = (Θ(V, ϕ, Λ, 0)(ȳ))⁻¹ for y ∈ H¹(ϕ^#(−f(β)), Λ^#)   (12.11).

items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) items.name: Definition 12.13: the involution σ on E
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) items.name: Full self-dual pss-characters; Ps₋(F^alg) and E₋
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) Self-dual semisimple strata/characters are those fixed by the adjoint anti-involution/σ as in §§8–9. A self-dual pss-character or endo-class is full if its lift is full; a self-dual semisimple character is full if it lies in C₋(Λ, 0, β) for a self-dual semisimple stratum [Λ, n, 0, β]. For a self-dual semisimple pair (0, β) with index set I = I₀ ∪ I₊ ∪ I₋ (I₀ the σ-fixed points, I₊ a section of the 2-element σ-orbits, I₋ = σ(I₊)), Ps₋(F^alg) is the set of full self-dual pss-characters Θ₋ whose pair (0, β) satisfies |I₀ ∪ I₊| = 1 and E ⊆ ⊕_{i∈I} F^alg; when I₊ ≠ ∅ write I₊ = {+1}, I₋ = {−1} and Θ_{±1} for the simple block restrictions of the lift Θ. E₋ is the set of endo-classes of elements of Ps₋(F^alg).

If Θ is not simple then [Θ₁] ≠ [Θ₋₁] = σ([Θ₁]).

items.name: Lemma 12.14(ii): a simple lift is σ-fixed

items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) items.name: Lemma 12.17: making a Σ-stable set of semisimple characters come from a self-dual stratum
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) Let (V, h) be an ε-hermitian space over F/F_o with a complete polarization V = V₁ ⊕ V₋₁ (12.18). Suppose [Λ, n, r, β] is a semisimple stratum split by (12.18) such that Λ is self-dual, C(Λ, r, β) = C(Λ, r, −β̄), and [Λ₁, n, r, β₁] is simple. Then there exists a self-dual semisimple stratum [Λ, n, r, β′] split by (12.18) such that C(Λ, r, β) = C(Λ, r, β′).

items.name: Definition 12.19: Witt types [β, t]
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) Consider pairs (β, t) where (0, β) is a self-dual simple pair and t ∈ W_ε(E/E_o), E = F[β]. Two pairs (β, t), (β′, t′) are equivalent if (i) (F[β], β) and (F[β′], β′) are similar self-dual extensions (Definition 3.33) and (ii) w_{ε,β′,β}(t) = t′. The equivalence classes are called Witt types; [β, t] is the class of (β, t).

items.name: Remarks 12.20(i): Witt-type equivalence via anisotropic parity and transfer (non-symplectic case)
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) In the non-symplectic case (F/F_o quadratic or ε = 1), for similar self-dual extensions (F[β], β), (F[β′], β′), condition (ii) of Definition 12.19 is equivalent to: the anisotropic dimensions of t and t′ have the same parity and λ*_β(t) = λ*_{β′}(t′).

items.name: WT(O): admissible Witt types for an orbit O ∈ E/Σ
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) Self-dual semisimple strata/characters are those fixed by the adjoint anti-involution/σ as in §§8–9. Identify E₋ with E/Σ via Φ (Theorem 12.16); for O ∈ E/Σ write [Θ₋] = Φ⁻¹(O) and deg(O) = deg(Θ₋), so deg(O) = |O|·deg(Θ_O) for any pss-character Θ_O with endo-class in O. Define WT(O) := {[β, t] | there is Θ₋ supported on (0, β) with Φ([Θ₋]) = O, t ∈ W_ε(F[β]/F[β]_o)} if |O| = 1, and WT(O) := {[0, 0]} if |O| = 2.

items.name: Remark 12.21: WT(O) ≅ W_ε(F[β]/F[β]_o) for |O| = 1

items.name: EP(O) and Definition 12.22: anisotropic dimension, degree and hermitian invariant of z
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) items.name: Definition 12.23: self-dual endo-parameter, its degree and hermitian invariant
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) Self-dual semisimple strata/characters are those fixed by the adjoint anti-involution/σ as in §§8–9. A self-dual endo-parameter (with respect to (F/F_o, ε)) is a section f₋ of ⊔_{O∈E/Σ} EP(O) → E/Σ with finite support supp(f₋) = {O ∈ E/Σ | deg(f₋(O)) ≠ 0}. Its degree is deg(f₋) = Σ_{O∈E/Σ} deg(f₋(O)) ∈ ℕ₀ and herm_{F/F_o}(f₋) = Σ_{O∈E/Σ} herm_{F/F_o}(f₋(O)) ∈ W_ε(F/F_o).

items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) items.name: Lemma 12.26: self-dual analogue of Lemma 12.4
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) Self-dual semisimple strata/characters are those fixed by the adjoint anti-involution/σ as in §§8–9. Let [Λ, n, r, β] and [Λ, n, r+1, γ] be self-dual semisimple strata split by V = V¹ ⊥ V² such that [Λ, n, r+1, β] is equivalent to [Λ, n, r+1, γ]. Put Λ^j = Λ ∩ V^j, β^j = β|_{V^j}. Given θ̃ ∈ C^Σ(Λ, r+1, γ) and an extension θ¹ ∈ C^Σ(Λ¹, r, β¹) of θ̃|_{H^{r+2}(β¹,Λ¹)}, there is θ ∈ C^Σ(Λ, r, β) whose restriction to H^{r+1}(β¹, Λ¹) is θ¹ and whose restriction to H^{r+2}(β, Λ) is θ̃.

items.name: Lemma 12.27: gluing self-dual semisimple characters on an orthogonal sum
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) Self-dual semisimple strata/characters are those fixed by the adjoint anti-involution/σ as in §§8–9. Let (V¹, h¹), (V², h²) be ε-hermitian spaces and θ¹ ∈ C^Σ(Λ¹, r, β¹), θ² ∈ C^Σ(Λ², r, β²) characters for self-dual semisimple strata in V¹, V² with e(Λ¹) = e(Λ²). Set V = V¹ ⊥ V², Λ = Λ¹ ⊕ Λ², n = max{n₁, n₂}. Then there exist self-dual semisimple strata [Λ¹, n₁, r, β̃¹] and [Λ², n₂, r, β̃²] in V¹, V² such that [Λ, n, r, β̃¹ ⊕ β̃²] is self-dual semisimple and there is θ ∈ C^Σ(Λ, r, β̃¹ ⊕ β̃²) with θ|_{H^{r+1}(β̃¹,Λ¹)} = θ¹ and θ|_{H^{r+1}(β̃²,Λ²)} = θ². Moreover β̃¹, β̃² can be chosen with the same associated splittings as β¹, β².

items.name: Definition 12.28: EP(h, G) and the endo-parameter f_{θ₋}
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) Self-dual semisimple strata/characters are those fixed by the adjoint anti-involution/σ as in §§8–9. EP(h, G) is the set of self-dual endo-parameters f₋ with herm_{F/F_o}(f₋) = [h] (the anisotropic class of h) and deg(f₋) = dim_F V. For a self-dual semisimple character θ₋ ∈ C₋(Λ, 0, β), let Θ₋ be the self-dual pss-character supported on (0, β) with value θ₋ at ((V, h), ϕ_β, Λ, 0), with lift Θ and index set I = I₀ ∪ I₊ ∪ I₋, so F₋([Θ₋]) = {O_i | i ∈ I₀ ∪ I₊} with O_i the orbit of [Θ_i]. Then f_{θ₋} has support F₋([Θ₋]) and f_{θ₋}(O_i) := ([β_i, [h_{id_{E_i}}]], m_i) for i ∈ I₀, f_{θ₋}(O_i) := ([0, 0], m_i) for i ∈ I₊, where h_{id_{E_i}} is the ε-hermitian form over E_i/E_{i,o} of Lemma 3.17, m_i is its Witt index (i ∈ I₀) and m_i = dim_{E_i}(V^i) (i ∈ I₊). The map θ₋ ↦ f_{θ₋} depends on h, not only on its isometry class.

items.name: Theorem 12.29: self-dual endo-parameters classify G-intertwining classes of full self-dual semisimple characters
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) items.name: Example (§12.4): dependence of f_{θ₋} on h rather than its isometry class
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) Self-dual semisimple strata/characters are those fixed by the adjoint anti-involution/σ as in §§8–9. Suppose −1 is not a square in F, (V, h) is symplectic and ϕ : E ↪ End_F(V) is a self-dual embedding of a self-dual extension (E, β) with dim_E V odd; let θ₋ ∈ C₋(Λ, 0, ϕ(β)). Then G = U(V, h) = U(V, −h) and EP(h, G) = EP(−h, G), but [h_ϕ] ≠ [−h_ϕ] = [(−h)_ϕ] 'because −1 ∉ N_{E/E_o}(E)', so the G-intertwining class of θ₋ is attached to different self-dual endo-parameters in EP(h, G) and in EP(−h, G).

items.name: Counting formula: number N(θ₋, G̃, G) of G-intertwining classes in a G̃-class
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) Self-dual semisimple strata/characters are those fixed by the adjoint anti-involution/σ as in §§8–9. Let θ ∈ C(Λ, 0, β) be the lift of a full self-dual semisimple character θ₋ ∈ C₋(Λ, 0, β), and N(θ₋, G̃, G) the number of G-intertwining classes of self-dual semisimple characters whose lift is in the G̃-intertwining class of θ (= number of f₋ ∈ EP(h, G) with the same GL-endo-parameter). Put n₀ := 0 if G is symplectic and β has no zero component; n₀ := 2 if G is orthogonal and β has a zero component β_{i₀} with dim_F V^{i₀} ≤ 2 and dim_an V^{i₀} ≤ 1; n₀ := 1 otherwise. Then N(θ₋, G̃, G) = 2^{max(|I₀| − n₀, 0)}. (The paper prints 2^{|I₀| − n₀}, which is not an integer in the two cases where |I₀| − n₀ = −1; see E36.)

items.name: Definition 12.30: (1 + p_F)-equivalence of symplectic forms
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) (Orthogonal case: ε = 1, F = F_o.) Two symplectic forms over F on an even-dimensional F-vector space V are (1 + p_F)-equivalent if they are isometric by an automorphism of V of determinant in 1 + p_F; [h′]_{1+p_F} denotes the class of a symplectic form h′.

items.name: Definition 12.31: embeddings adapted to f₋, f_{ϕ,−} and the set H(f₋)
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) (Orthogonal case: ε = 1, F = F_o.) Let f₋ ∈ EP(h, G) and Θ₋ a self-dual pss-character supported on some (0, β) with F₋([Θ₋]) = supp(f₋); I = I₊ ∪ I₀ ∪ I₋, E = F[β], F₋([Θ₋]) = {O_i | i ∈ I₀ ∪ I₊}. For a self-dual embedding ϕ : E → End_F V with decomposition V = ⊕_{i∈I} V^i, f_{ϕ,−} is the endo-parameter for (h, G) with support F₋([Θ₋]) and f_{ϕ,−}(O_i) := ([β_i, [h_{i,ϕ_i}]], m_i) for i ∈ I₀ (m_i the Witt index of h_{i,ϕ_i}), f_{ϕ,−}(O_i) := ([0, 0], m_i) for i ∈ I₊ (m_i = dim_{E_i} V^i); ϕ is adapted to f₋ if f₋ = f_{ϕ,−}. If the zero endo-class is not in supp(f₋), H(f₋) := {[ϕ(β)*h]_{1+p_F} | ϕ an embedding adapted to f₋}; otherwise H(f₋) := {0}.

items.name: Lemma 12.32: H(f₋) is independent of Θ₋ and has two elements when non-trivial
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) (Orthogonal case: ε = 1, F = F_o.) For f₋ ∈ EP(h, G), the set H(f₋) does not depend on the choice of the self-dual pss-character Θ₋; moreover, H(f₋) has cardinality two whenever it is non-trivial.

items.name: Definition 12.33: endo-parameters EP(h, G°) for special orthogonal groups, and h_{θ₋}
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) items.name: The lattice m_r(β, Λ) and the group S_r(β, Λ)
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p (a finite extension of F_o as in §2); V a finite-dimensional F-vector space, G̃ = GL_F(V) = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) For a non-null semisimple stratum [Λ, n, r, β] with k₀ = k₀(β, Λ): n_{−r}(β, Λ) = {a ∈ a₀(Λ) | βa − aβ ∈ a_{−r}}, m_r(β, Λ) = n_{−r}(β, Λ) ∩ a_{−(r+k₀)}(Λ). The pro-p subgroup 1 + m_r(β, Λ) of P_{−k₀−r}(Λ) normalizes the equivalence class of the stratum and every character in C(Λ, r, β); S_r(β, Λ) = 1 + m_r(β, Λ) + J^{⌊(−k₀+1)/2⌋}(β, Λ) also normalizes every character in C(Λ, r, β) ([42, Lemma 3.16]).

items.name: Theorem A.1: translation principle for self-dual semisimple characters
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) Self-dual semisimple strata/characters are those fixed by the adjoint anti-involution/σ as in §§8–9. Let [Λ, n, r+1, γ] and [Λ, n, r+1, γ′] be self-dual semisimple strata with the same associated splitting V = ⊕_{j∈J} V^j such that C(Λ, r+1, γ) = C(Λ, r+1, γ′). Let [Λ, n, r, β] be a self-dual semisimple stratum with associated splitting V = ⊕_{i∈I} V^i such that [Λ, n, r+1, β] is equivalent to [Λ, n, r+1, γ] and γ ∈ ∏_{i∈I} A^i. Then there exist a self-dual semisimple stratum [Λ, n, r, β′], with splitting V = ⊕_{i′∈I′} V′^{i′}, and u ∈ (1 + m_{r+1}(γ, Λ)) ∩ ∏_{j∈J} A^j ∩ G such that [Λ, n, r+1, β′] is equivalent to [Λ, n, r+1, γ′], uγ′u⁻¹ ∈ ∏_{i′∈I′} A′^{i′}, and C(Λ, r, β) = C(Λ, r, β′).

items.name: Lemma A.2 ([39, Lemma 7.13]): lifting an approximate idempotent, symmetric if α is
items.statement: Let A be as in KSS (a finite-dimensional F-algebra with anti-involution x ↦ x̄) and (k_r)_{r≥0} a decreasing sequence of σ-invariant (¯-stable) o_F-lattices in A with k_r k_s ⊆ k_{r+s} for all r, s ≥ 0 and ∩_{r≥1} k_r = {0}. If α ∈ k₀ satisfies α² − α ∈ k₁, there is an idempotent α̃ ∈ α + k₁; if moreover ᾱ = α, α̃ can be chosen with ᾱ̃ = α̃.

items.name: Lemma A.3: lifting to an idempotent orthogonal to its adjoint
items.statement: In the setting of Lemma A.2, suppose α ∈ k₀ satisfies α² − α ∈ k₁ and αᾱ, ᾱα ∈ k₁. Then there is an idempotent α̃ ∈ α + k₁ such that α̃ᾱ̃ = ᾱ̃α̃ = 0.
items.note: Missing; see Lemma A.2 note. Checked: α₁ = e(1+α−ᾱ)/2 e satisfies α₁ + ᾱ₁ = e, and f(x) = 3x² − 2x³ satisfies f(x) + f(e − x) = e.

items.name: Corollary A.4: lifting a σ-compatible complete family of approximate orthogonal idempotents
items.statement: In the setting of Lemma A.2, let α₁, …, α_l ∈ k₀ with α_i² − α_i, α_iα_j ∈ k₁ for all i ≠ j, Σ_i α_i − 1 ∈ k₁, and suppose σ acts on I = {1, …, l} with ᾱ_i − α_{σ(i)} ∈ k₁ for all i. Then there are pairwise orthogonal idempotents α̃_i ∈ α_i + k₁ with Σ_i α̃_i = 1 and ᾱ̃_i = α̃_{σ(i)} for all i ∈ I.

items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) Suppose [Λ, n, r, β] is split by V = ⊕_{k∈K} V^k and the set of idempotents of this splitting is invariant under ¯. Then there is u ∈ (1 + m_r(β, Λ)) ∩ G such that uβ′u⁻¹ ∈ ∏_{k∈K} A^k.

items.name: Lemma A.7(i) (cf. [39, Lemma 9.13]): twisting by ψ_a on blocks yields a semisimple stratum
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p (a finite extension of F_o as in §2); V a finite-dimensional F-vector space, G̃ = GL_F(V) = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) Let V = ⊕_{k∈K} V^k be a splitting refining the associated splitting of a semisimple stratum [Λ, n, r, β], with idempotents e_k and β_k = e_kβe_k. Let θ ∈ C(Λ, r, β) with restrictions θ_k ∈ C(Λ^k, r, β_k) and, for k ∈ K, let a_k ∈ a_{−r−1} ∩ A^k be such that θ_kψ_{a_k} ∈ C(Λ^k, r, β_k); put a = Σ_k a_k. Then [Λ, n, r, β + a] is equivalent to a semisimple stratum [Λ, n, r, β′] split by V = ⊕_k V^k, and C(Λ, r, β′) = ψ_a C(Λ, r, β).

items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p (a finite extension of F_o as in §2); V a finite-dimensional F-vector space, G̃ = GL_F(V) = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) Suppose V = ⊕_k V^k is a splitting refining the associated splittings of two semisimple strata [Λ, n, r, β] and [Λ, n, r, β′], and there are θ ∈ C(Λ, r, β), θ′ ∈ C(Λ, r, β′) with θ_k = θ′_k for all k. items.name: Proposition A.9(i) ([39, Proposition 9.9(iv)]): S_r(β, Λ) moves the splitting of β to that of β′
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p (a finite extension of F_o as in §2); V a finite-dimensional F-vector space, G̃ = GL_F(V) = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) Suppose C(Λ, r, β) = C(Λ, r, β′) and let τ : I → I′ be the bijection of [39, Proposition 9.9] with e_i ≡ e′_{τ(i)} (mod a₁(Λ)). Then there is g ∈ S_r(β, Λ) with g e_i g⁻¹ = e′_{τ(i)} for all i ∈ I (and g normalizes every element of C(Λ, r, β)).

items.name: Lemma A.11(i) (cf. [39, Proposition 9.17]): intertwiners factor through G̃_γ and intertwine derived strata
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p (a finite extension of F_o as in §2); V a finite-dimensional F-vector space, G̃ = GL_F(V) = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) Suppose m < q − 1 and let [Λ, q, m, β], [Λ′, q, m, β′] be semisimple strata with e(Λ) = e(Λ′) and splittings V = ⊕_{i∈I} V^i, V = ⊕_{i∈I′} V′^i. Suppose [Λ, q, m+1, γ] and [Λ′, q, m+1, γ] are non-null simple strata equivalent to [Λ, q, m+1, β] and [Λ′, q, m+1, β′] respectively, with γ ∈ ⊕_{i∈I} A^i ∩ ⊕_{i′∈I′} A′^{i′}. Let θ₀ ∈ C(Λ, m, γ), θ′₀ = τ_{Λ′,Λ,γ}(θ₀) ∈ C(Λ′, m, γ), and θ ∈ C(Λ, m, β), θ′ ∈ C(Λ′, m, β′) with θ = θ₀ψ_{β−γ+c}, θ′ = θ′₀ψ_{β′−γ} for some c ∈ a_{−(m+1)}; let s_γ be a tame corestriction for γ. Then every g ∈ I_{G̃}(θ, θ′) can be written g = xg′y with x ∈ S_{m+1}(γ, Λ′), y ∈ S_{m+1}(γ, Λ), g′ ∈ G̃_γ, and g′ intertwines [Λ, m+1, m, s_γ(β−γ+c)] with [Λ′, m+1, m, s_γ(β′−γ)].

items.name: Theorem A.13: intertwining implies conjugacy for self-dual semisimple characters
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) Self-dual semisimple strata/characters are those fixed by the adjoint anti-involution/σ as in §§8–9. Let [Λ, n, r, β] and [Λ, n, r, β′] be self-dual semisimple strata in A and let θ ∈ C₋(Λ, r, β), θ′ ∈ C₋(Λ, r, β′) be self-dual semisimple characters which intertwine in G and whose matching ζ : I → I′ ([39, Theorem 10.1]) satisfies Λ^i(j)/Λ^i(j+1) ≅ Λ^{ζ(i)}(j)/Λ^{ζ(i)}(j+1) for all i ∈ I and all integers j. Then there is an element of P₋(Λ) ∩ ∏_{i∈I} Hom_F(V^i, V′^{ζ(i)}) which conjugates θ to θ′.

items.name: External [39, Theorem 9.16]: translation principle for semisimple characters of G̃
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p (a finite extension of F_o as in §2); V a finite-dimensional F-vector space, G̃ = GL_F(V) = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) Given semisimple strata [Λ, n, r+1, γ], [Λ, n, r+1, γ′] with C(Λ, r+1, γ) = C(Λ, r+1, γ′) and a semisimple stratum [Λ, n, r, β] with [Λ, n, r+1, β] equivalent to [Λ, n, r+1, γ], there is a semisimple stratum [Λ, n, r, β′] with [Λ, n, r+1, β′] equivalent to [Λ, n, r+1, γ′] and C(Λ, r, β) = C(Λ, r, β′) (with the conjugation property on splittings, as in Theorem A.1).

items.name: External [39, Theorem 8.1]: intertwining simple strata are P(Λ)-conjugate up to equivalence
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p (a finite extension of F_o as in §2); V a finite-dimensional F-vector space, G̃ = GL_F(V) = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) items.name: External [26, Theorem 2.12]: the cohomology (Glauberman-type) argument for Σ-fixed double cosets
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) For a pro-p group K with an action of Σ (p odd) and Σ-stable closed subgroups, the Σ-fixed points of a product decomposition of intertwining sets descend: e.g. (S_r(β,Λ′) G̃_β S_r(β,Λ))^Σ = (S_r(β,Λ′) ∩ G) G_β (S_r(β,Λ) ∩ G) (form used in Proposition A.10(ii)).
items.locator: used in Proposition A.10(ii), p. 78 (Kurinczuk–Stevens [26, Theorem 2.12]; cf. [40, Corollary 4.14]), arXiv:1611.02667v3
items.note: Missing. Non-abelian cohomology of Σ = ℤ/2 acting on pro-p groups (Glauberman's lemma) is not in Mathlib/Tau Ceti; Tau Ceti ProfiniteCohomology plans abelian continuous cohomology only. Recorded in the form used.

items.name: External [13, Lemma 5.2]: compatible tame corestrictions
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p (a finite extension of F_o as in §2); V a finite-dimensional F-vector space, G̃ = GL_F(V) = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) For simple strata with C(Λ, r, γ) = C(Λ, r, γ′) there are tame corestrictions s, s′ for γ, γ′ with s(x) ≡ s′(x) (mod a_l) for all x ∈ a_{l−1} and all l, and (in the self-dual case) commuting with the adjoint anti-involution; and the canonical embeddings of k_{F[γ]} and k_{F[γ′]} into a₀/a₁ have the same image.

items.name: Extended Langlands parameters (ϱ, χ_ϱ) and Lang(G°)
items.statement: An (extended) Langlands parameter for G° is a pair (ϱ, χ_ϱ) where (i) ϱ : W′_{F_o} → ^L G° is a continuous homomorphism such that (a) ϱ(I_{F_o}) is finite, ϱ is Frobenius-semisimple and ϱ|_{SL₂(ℂ)} : SL₂(ℂ) → Ĝ° is algebraic, (b) the composition W_{F_o} → ^L G° → W_{F_o} is the identity; (ii) χ_ϱ is an irreducible complex representation of S_ϱ := C_{Ĝ°}(ϱ(W′_{F_o}))/C_{Ĝ°}(ϱ(W′_{F_o}))° Z(Ĝ°)^{W_{F_o}}. Lang(G°) is the set of Ĝ°-conjugacy classes of such pairs.
items.note: Missing. Nearest: LanglandsParameterStacks LP0 (L-parameters as continuous 1-cocycles W_E → Ĝ, sections of the L-group projection), ExcursionOperatorsAndSpectralAction ES5 (Fargues–Scholze semisimple parameter φ_π for any G, explicitly 'not a nilpotent monodromy operator, packets, surjectivity or categorical LLC'), and ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.4 (Arthur/Mok packets as registered sources). Component groups S_ϱ and their characters are planned nowhere.

items.name: External (Arthur [2], Mok [30], Ganapathy–Varma [21], KMSW [25]): local Langlands correspondence for classical groups
items.statement: Let F_o be a non-archimedean local field (of characteristic 0 for [2], [30]) and G° a quasi-split classical group over F_o. Fixing a non-degenerate character of the unipotent radical of a Borel subgroup of G°, there is a natural bijection LL : Irr(G°) → Lang(G°) (Irr(G°) = isomorphism classes of irreducible smooth complex representations); known for tempered representations of split classical groups [2] and quasi-split unitary groups [30] in characteristic 0, extended to some positive characteristics for split classical groups [21], with work in progress for inner forms of unitary groups [25].
items.locator: §1.20, p. 8 (LL is predicted in general; known cases as listed), arXiv:1611.02667v3
items.note: Planned (as registered source input): ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.4 'Give Arthur/Mok/KMSW classification inputs explicit proof-source owners: stabilization, transfer, fundamental lemma, packets, multiplicities and local-global compatibilities', preserving conditional hypotheses; ML.5 registers frontier/conditional statements. Not covered: the positive-characteristic extension [21], the full (non-tempered) LL, and the normalization via extended parameters (ϱ, χ_ϱ). The proposed GanGrossPrasadConjecturesForClassicalGroups and GSp4LocalLanglandsAndGaloisRepresentations Part II roadmaps (not in the atlas) import local packets from the same Arthur/Mok sources. This is where KSS's remark 'L-packets for classical groups are not singletons' (§1.4) would land.

items.name: Wild inertial parameters, S_ρ, extended wild inertial parameters, Wild(G°) and Res
items.statement: A wild inertial parameter for G° is a homomorphism ρ : P_{F_o} → ^L G° which extends to a Langlands parameter ϱ : W′_{F_o} → ^L G°. Put C_{^L G°}(ρ) = {(g, w) ∈ ^L G° | (g, w)ρ(w⁻¹pw)(g, w)⁻¹ = ρ(p) for all p ∈ P_{F_o}} ≅ C_{Ĝ°}(ρ) ⋊_{Ad ϱ} W_{F_o}, so that Z(Ĝ°)^{W_{F_o}} ≤ Z(C_{^L G°}(ρ)) ≅ Z(C_{Ĝ°}(ρ))^{ϱ(W_{F_o})} ≤ C_{Ĝ°}(ϱ(W′_{F_o})) (1.1), and S_ρ := Z(C_{^L G°}(ρ))/Z(Ĝ°)^{W_{F_o}}. An extended wild inertial parameter is a pair (ρ, χ_ρ) with χ_ρ a representation of S_ρ such that (ρ, χ_ρ) = (ϱ|_{P_{F_o}}, χ_ϱ|_{Z(C_{^L G°}(ρ))}) for some extended Langlands parameter (ϱ, χ_ϱ). Wild(G°) is the set of Ĝ°-conjugacy classes of these, and Res : Lang(G°) → Wild(G°), (ϱ, χ_ϱ) ↦ (ϱ|_{P_{F_o}}, χ_ϱ|_{Z(C_{^L G°}(ρ))}).
items.note: Missing. LanglandsParameterStacks LP1 ('decomposition by wild kernel', finite-wild pieces Z¹(W_E/P, Ĝ)) and SR.6 (Dat–Helm–Kurinczuk–Moss finite-wild cocycle schemes) are the nearest: they treat parameters trivial on an open subgroup of wild inertia, not restriction to P_{F_o} with the centralizer-centre character data.

items.name: The map ϑ : Irr(G°) → EP(h, G°)
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) (C = ℂ.) ϑ takes π ∈ Irr(G°) to the self-dual endo-parameter (Theorem 12.29 / Corollary 12.34) attached to the intertwining class of any full self-dual semisimple character contained in π; it depends on the hermitian form h. (Every π contains such a character by [16, Proposition 8.5]; any two contained in π intertwine, hence give the same endo-parameter.)
items.note: Missing. Self-dual endo-classes/endo-parameters of classical groups have no atlas owner and no proposal covers them. Witt groups of ε-hermitian forms and the transfer λ* are at most stage-level in GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.2 ('Witt groups … quaternionic/hermitian variants'); Tau Ceti has the Witt decomposition, Witt index and anisotropic part only for quadratic forms over a field with 2 invertible (tauceti:TauCeti.RegularFormClass.wittIndex, tauceti:TauCeti.RegularFormClass.anisotropicPart), not for ε-hermitian forms over E/E_o.

items.name: Conjecture (Wild local Langlands): EP(h, G°) ≅ Wild(G°) compatibly with LLC
items.statement: (Standing hypotheses of KSS: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p; F/F_o is an extension of degree ≤ 2 with involution x ↦ x̄; (V, h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space over F/F_o (ε = ±1); G̃ = Aut_F(V), A = End_F(V), a ↦ ā the adjoint anti-involution of h, σ(g) = ḡ⁻¹, Σ = {1, σ}; G = U(V, h) = G̃^Σ and G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V, h) in the orthogonal case, the F_o-points of a unitary, symplectic or special orthogonal group, G° ≇ SO(1,1)(F_o); characters take values in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p.) (C = ℂ; G° quasi-split.) There is a unique bijection LL_p : EP(h, G°) → Wild(G°) compatible with the local Langlands correspondence, i.e. such that the diagram (1.2) commutes: Res ∘ LL = LL_p ∘ ϑ as maps Irr(G°) → Wild(G°), where EP(h, G°) is the set of self-dual endo-parameters for G° ⊆ U(V, h) (§12.4, and §12.5 in the special orthogonal case).
items.locator: §1.21, Conjecture (Wild local Langlands) and diagram (1.2), p. 9 (stated in the introduction; parameters from §12), arXiv:1611.02667v3
items.note: Conjecture — recorded, not a target. No atlas owner: it needs the classical-group LL (only registered as source in ML.4), Wild(G°) (not planned) and EP(h, G°) (not planned). ES5's Fargues–Scholze semisimple parameter restricted to P_{F_o} would give the non-extended wild parameter for any G, but its compatibility with Arthur's LL for classical groups is not planned. The GL analogue is Bushnell–Henniart's ramification theorem (see item). Overlaps the introduction range of another reader.

items.name: External [4, Theorem 7.6] (Blondel–Henniart–Stevens): the conjecture for cuspidal representations of symplectic groups, up to Witt data and extension
items.statement: Assume LL for symplectic groups. For cuspidal representations of symplectic groups G° = Sp(V), after forgetting the Witt-type data of self-dual endo-parameters (with ϑ defined via Theorem 12.29) and projecting Wild(G°) to non-extended wild parameters, the resulting map is a bijection making the diagram (1.2) commute.
items.locator: §1.21, p. 9 (Blondel–Henniart–Stevens [4, Theorem 7.6]; cf. [4, Theorem 7.1] in §1.3), arXiv:1611.02667v3
items.note: Missing; external result, conditional on LL. Nothing in the atlas plans Jordan blocks of cuspidal representations of symplectic groups.

items.name: External (Bushnell–Henniart [10, 6.1 Theorem]): ramification theorem — GL endo-classes ↔ wild inertia
items.statement: Let F be a non-archimedean local field. Under the local Langlands correspondence for GL_n(F), the endo-class of an irreducible cuspidal representation π of GL_n(F) determines, and is determined by, the restriction to the wild inertia subgroup P_F of the Langlands parameter of π up to conjugacy; this gives a bijection between E and W_F-orbits of irreducible representations of P_F (the GL-prototype of the wild local Langlands conjecture).
items.note: Missing. LLC for GL_m is planned in EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.6 (mixed characteristic E/ℚ_p, full WD parameters) and compared with Fargues–Scholze in ES7:GLn-comparison, but no stage states the ramification theorem. The rejected PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17 proposal lists the nearest items ('wild-llc', 'first-ramification', 'truncated-class-to-orbit', 'llc-char0' → ET.6).

items.name: External: local Langlands correspondence for GL_n (input to the GL interpretation of endo-parameters)
items.statement: For E/ℚ_p finite there is a bijection between irreducible smooth complex representations of GL_n(E) and n-dimensional Frobenius-semisimple Weil–Deligne representations of W_E, compatible with L- and ε-factors of pairs, twists, central characters and duals (Harris–Taylor, Henniart, Scholze).
items.note: Planned: EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.6 constructs the characteristic-zero LLC for GL_m(E), E/ℚ_p, with full WD parameters (Scholze's route); equal characteristic is explicitly excluded there. Used by KSS only as motivation for interpreting GL endo-parameters.

routes.title: Smooth representations of local groups, Part II: semisimple characters, cuspidal types and endo-parameters for p-adic classical groups
routes.brief: This route coalesces with SmoothRepresentationsPartII, proposed by PAPER-FINTZEN-21 (types, depth and the construction of supercuspidal representations) and continued by other extractions; keep that id and parent. It adds a separately scoped branch for p-adic classical groups after Bushnell–Kutzko and Stevens, from Kurinczuk, Skodlerack and Stevens, 'Endo-parameters for p-adic classical groups', Invent. Math. 223 (2021) (arXiv:1611.02667v3 numbering). Its hypotheses are not Fintzen's: F_o is a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic p (any p ≠ 2, no Weyl-group bound), F/F_o has degree ≤ 2 with involution, (V,h) is a non-degenerate ε-hermitian space, G = U(V,h), G° = G in the unitary and symplectic cases and G° = G ∩ SL_F(V) = SO(V,h) in the orthogonal case (not SO(1,1)), and coefficients lie in an algebraically closed field C of characteristic ≠ p. Final theorems, stated as the paper does: (1) Theorem 11.9: if two cuspidal types (J,λ), (J′,λ′) for G° intertwine in G°, they are conjugate in G°; hence, for cuspidal types with π_i ≅ ind_{J_i}^{G°} λ_i, π_1 ≅ π_2 iff there is g ∈ G° with J_1^g = J_2 and λ_1^g ≅ λ_2 (§1.4), completing the classification of irreducible cuspidal C-representations of G° by conjugacy classes of cuspidal types. (2) Theorems 9.9 and 9.16, Corollary 9.17: endo-equivalence of potential semisimple characters (pss-characters) of general linear groups, and of self-dual pss-characters of classical groups, is an equivalence relation, characterised componentwise through the unique matching and, in the self-dual case, through the lifts and ζ-concordance of the embeddings. (3) Theorem 12.9: intertwining classes of full semisimple characters of GL_F(V) are in canonical bijection with endo-parameters of degree dim_F V; Theorem 12.29: G-intertwining classes of full self-dual semisimple characters of U(V,h) are in canonical bijection with EP(h,G); Corollary 12.34: G°-intertwining classes in the special orthogonal case are in bijection with EP(h,G°). (4) Record, not prove: the Conjecture of §1.21 that there is a unique bijection EP(h,G°) → Wild(G°) compatible with the local Langlands correspondence (Res ∘ LL = LL_p ∘ ϑ), with the known symplectic cuspidal case of Blondel–Henniart–Stevens. Cover, in order: intertwining sets I_g, I_G (§2); self-dual extensions (E,β), their parity and similarity invariants, self-dual embeddings ϕ: E ↪ End_F(V) with the lifted forms h_ϕ, the comparison maps w_ε on Witt groups, and (h,h′)-concordance (§§3.1, 3.6–3.9); lattice sequences, hereditary orders, P(Λ), P_−(Λ), strata, simple, self-dual and semisimple strata with simple approximation and intertwining-implies-conjugacy for strata (§5); the groups H(β,Λ), simple and semisimple characters C(Λ,r,β) with transfer, the Glauberman correspondence C^Σ → C_−, and intertwining of self-dual simple characters (Proposition 6.10); ps- and pss-characters, their realizations and endo-equivalence (§§7, 9); the matching theorem and intertwining implies conjugacy for self-dual semisimple characters (§8, Theorems 8.8, 8.15, 8.17) with Appendix A's translation principle; the special orthogonal refinements (§10); cuspidal types, β-extensions and the proof of Theorem 11.9 (§11); endo-parameters, Witt types and EP(h,G), EP(h,G°) (§12). Import, never rebuild: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups SR.0–SR.2 (smooth category, compact induction, Frobenius reciprocity and Mackey theory); EndoscopicTransferAndUnitaryTraceComparison ET.6 for GL_m types and the classical GL_m local Langlands correspondence (which the reviews of PAPER-FINTZEN-21 and PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17 assign GL_m type theory to) — the Bushnell–Kutzko simple strata and simple characters of GL_N are shared with the GL_n endo-class branch proposed by PAPER-BUSHNELL-HENNIART-17 and must be planned once; ReductiveGroupsPartII (buildings and parahorics, compared with lattice sequences); GeometryOfNumbersAndQuadraticArithmetic GN.2 (ε-hermitian spaces, Witt groups, and the transfer routed there from this paper); the Tau Ceti roadmaps LocalFieldsRamification and ClassFieldTheory (local fields, norm groups, Weil group and wild inertia); ModularityAndLanglandsExtensions ML.4 and LanglandsParameterStacks LP0 for the parameter side of the conjecture. Coordinate with the extraction of Stevens, 'The supercuspidal representations of p-adic classical groups' (PAPER-STEVENS-08), which supplies the construction of cuspidal types this branch classifies. Carry the corrections recorded in sourceIssues (Theorem 10.4's conjugating element, Corollary 8.19, the counting formula of §12.4, the example after Theorem 12.29, and the example of §10.2, which holds as printed only for r = 0). Tests: Sp_2 = SL_2 and its depth-zero and simple cuspidal types; U(1,1) for an unramified quadratic F/F_o; SO_3 ≅ PGL_2 and SO_4, where G°-conjugacy differs from G-conjugacy (§10); the example after Theorem 12.29 showing EP(h,G) depends on h; and the GL_1 case, where endo-parameters are characters of wild inertia.
routes.reason: SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups plans the smooth category, Hecke algebras, compact induction and the Bernstein decomposition (SR.0–SR.3) but no types. The Part II proposed by PAPER-FINTZEN-21 plans Kim–Yu types and Yu's construction under p not dividing the Weyl-group order and complex coefficients, and the reviewed proposals assign GL_m type theory to ET.6; nothing in the atlas or its proposals plans strata, simple or semisimple characters of classical groups, cuspidal types for classical groups in all odd p with modular coefficients, endo-classes or endo-parameters. The maintainer's note for this paper asks for exactly this: a Part II of SmoothRepresentationsOfLocalGroups for types and semisimple characters of classical groups, endo-parameters and their relation to L-packets, reusing the local Langlands and parameter roadmaps. Since make_queue plans all Part IIs of one parent as one roadmap, the branch joins SmoothRepresentationsPartII rather than proposing a second types roadmap.

GN.2 integrates Witt groups, discriminants, invariants and local classification of quadratic forms and asks for their 'quaternionic/hermitian variants'; the paper's §§3.1–3.5 are that hermitian local theory over a quadratic or trivial extension F/F_o of a non-archimedean local field of odd residual characteristic: norm groups of quadratic extensions (Lemma 3.1), the unitary group of an ε-hermitian space and the twisted forms a^*(h) (§3.3), the twisting isomorphisms of the Witt groups W^ε(F/F_o) (§3.4), and the transfer λ_*: W^ε(E/E_o) → W^ε(F/F_o) along a Galois-equivariant linear form with Propositions 3.13–3.15 (image independent of λ, maximal elements, injectivity on parity classes, determinant, the standard transfer), which extend Scharlau's transfer of quadratic forms. They belong inside GN.2 next to the Witt groups themselves, which this extraction already marks as planned there; the Tau Ceti QuadraticFormInvariants roadmap (Layer 9) supplies the quadratic case of the transfer.

LP0 constructs Weil groups with inertia and wild inertia, continuous cocycles and sections of the L-group projection, and states that finite wild ramification means triviality on an open subgroup of wild inertia. The paper's wild inertial parameters — restrictions ρ = ϱ|_{P_{F_o}} of Langlands parameters, the centralizers C_{^LG°}(ρ) ≅ C_{Ĝ°}(ρ) ⋊ W_{F_o}, the groups S_ρ, extended wild parameters, the set Wild(G°) and the restriction map Res (§1.21 with (1.1)) — are parameters restricted to wild inertia and belong with LP0's definitions.

ML.4 gives the Arthur, Mok and Kaletha–Mínguez–Shin–White classification its source owners, including packets and multiplicities. The paper's extended Langlands parameters (ϱ, χ_ϱ), with χ_ϱ a character of the component group S_ϱ, and the set Lang(G°) (§1.20) are the parametrisation of L-packets that this classification uses, and the local Langlands correspondence LL: Irr(G°) → Lang(G°) is already marked planned there.

The existence of a single l, which is all the argument as written yields, gives neither. Monotonicity in l does hold (rescale to level e, then lower the level with Proposition 5.5), but the proof does not say so. The subsequence version of the same argument also repairs it; either fix is a sentence.

Take self-dual realizations of Θ− and Θ′− on a common ε-hermitian space with all blocks of equal F-dimension, for example with hyperbolic E_i-forms on the I_0-blocks. By Theorem 9.9(ii)(b) take equal periods and levels. By Theorem 9.9(ii)(d) the σ-invariant lifts θ, θ′ intertwine with matching ζ. If g intertwines θ with θ′ with matching ζ, then σ(g) intertwines θ^σ = θ with θ′^σ = θ′ and maps V^{σ(i)} to V′^{σ(ζ(i))}, so σζσ is also a matching. sourceIssues.correction: Normalise first, as in the proof of Theorem 7.9: translate Λ, Λ′ affinely to e(Λ) = e(Λ′) and replace r, r′ by min{r, r′} using Theorem 9.9(ii)(b); intertwining with matching ζ passes back to the original restrictions. Alternatively cite Proposition 7.10 for the block ps-characters.
sourceIssues.reason: Proposition 6.10 assumes θ_− ∈ C_−(Λ, r, β), θ′_− ∈ C_−(Λ′, r, β′) with the same r and e(Λ) = e(Λ′). In (iii) the quadruples are arbitrary, so the block characters can have different levels and periods. The proof of Theorem 7.9 makes this normalisation explicitly; here it is omitted. The block ps-characters are endo-equivalent, so the repair is routine.

sourceIssues.locator: §10.2, first paragraph, p. 58, arXiv:1611.02667v3; p. 687 in the version of record
sourceIssues.printed: It assumes i₀ ∈ I with β_{i₀} = 0 and no determinant −1 element normalizing P₋(Λ^{i₀}), then takes g_{i₀} ∈ U(V^{i₀}, h_{i₀}) of determinant −1. It cites Theorem 10.2 for intertwining of θ with θ′ = ^gθ by an element of G°, but claims they are not conjugate in G°, referring to an exercise based on Proposition A.9(ii) together with Theorem 10.2.
sourceIssues.correction: Restrict the example to r = 0, or assume instead that the normalizer of P^{r+1}₋(Λ^{i₀}) (equivalently, of θ_{i₀}) in U(V^{i₀}, h_{i₀}) contains no element of determinant −1. The opening claim of §10.2, that such characters exist, is unaffected, since examples with r = 0 exist.
sourceIssues.reason: For r ≥ 1 and a non-strict Λ^{i₀}, P^{r+1}(Λ^{i₀}) can have a larger normalizer than P(Λ^{i₀}); the authors note this for O(1,1) in a commented-out remark before Remark 10.5. Counterexample: V = M₂(F) with the quadratic form det, so G° = SO(2,2) is split, its building is a product of two trees, and elements of determinant −1 (such as transposition τ) swap the trees. Take β = 0 (so I = {i₀}), r = 1, and the self-dual lattice sequence Λ of period 3 attached to the point (v₀, x) of the building, where v₀ is a vertex and x lies a third of the way along an edge. Then a₂(Λ) = ϖ_F End_{o_F}(M₂(o_F)), so P²(Λ) is the first congruence subgroup of the stabilizer of the lattice M₂(o_F), which τ normalizes, while no element of determinant −1 normalizes P₋(Λ), because it would move (v₀, x) to a point whose first coordinate is not a vertex. For the trivial character θ of P²(Λ) and any g of determinant −1, y = gτ ∈ G° satisfies ^yθ = ^gθ = θ′, so θ and θ′ are G°-conjugate.

review.reason: Found by the review. The review checked the key step on the building: in a tree, the Moy–Prasad group at depth 2/3 of a point a third of the way along an edge from a vertex v equals the depth-1 group of v, so P²(Λ) is the depth-1 group of a vertex of the product building, which transposition normalizes, while the facet of (v₀, x) is not symmetric in the two factors. The example is unchanged in the version of record.
